Diagnosis requires exclusion of secondary causes with neuroimaging and demonstration of elevated cerebrospinal-fluid opening pressure with otherwise normal CSF composition.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize idiopathic intracranial hypertension when headache and visual symptoms occur with papilledema and elevated CSF opening pressure after imaging excludes a mass, hydrocephalus, and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Endogenous pancreatic beta cells synthesize proinsulin and cleave it into insulin and C-peptide before secretion. Exogenous insulin provides insulin without accompanying C-peptide or proinsulin. Therefore, during hypoglycemia caused by exogenous insulin, circulating insulin is inappropriately elevated while endogenous C-peptide and proinsulin are suppressed. Insulin secretagogues and insulinoma instead stimulate endogenous insulin secretion and therefore raise C-peptide; a secretagogue screen helps distinguish medication ingestion from insulinoma.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate causes of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia using insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, and insulin-secretagogue testing: elevated insulin with suppressed C-peptide/proinsulin indicates exogenous insulin administration.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Failure to capture occurs when a pacemaker delivers an electrical pacing impulse but the myocardium does not depolarize in response. On the surface ECG, a pacing spike is present without a subsequent evoked P wave or QRS complex. This differs from output failure, in which the expected pacing spike is absent; undersensing, in which intrinsic depolarizations are not detected and pacing occurs inappropriately; and oversensing, in which non-target electrical signals inappropriately inhibit pacing.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize pacemaker failure to capture on ECG as a visible pacing spike that is not followed by the expected myocardial depolarization.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The 5 A's framework organizes tobacco-cessation counseling as Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, and Arrange. After tobacco use has been identified and the clinician has clearly advised cessation, the next step is to assess whether the patient is willing to make a quit attempt at this time. Assistance with a quit plan or pharmacotherapy follows for a patient who is willing, and follow-up is then arranged.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Apply the 5 A's tobacco-cessation framework in sequence: after identifying tobacco use and advising cessation, assess willingness to make a quit attempt before moving to assistance and follow-up.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Acquired hemophilia A results from an autoantibody that inhibits factor VIII. It should be suspected in a patient with new-onset bleeding and an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time. A factor deficiency is corrected by mixing patient plasma with normal plasma, whereas a clinically significant inhibitor prevents correction; factor VIII activity is reduced in acquired hemophilia A.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize acquired hemophilia A when new-onset bleeding is accompanied by isolated aPTT prolongation, reduced factor VIII activity, and failure of an incubated mixing study to correct, indicating a factor VIII inhibitor.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A run chart displays a measure in time order around a median. Run-chart rules are used to distinguish likely nonrandom change from ordinary variation. For a run chart with fewer than 20 data points, six or more consecutive points entirely above or below the median constitute a shift; points on the median are not counted. A shift is a signal that the underlying process may have changed and should be investigated in relation to interventions or other events.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Interpret a quality-improvement run chart: with fewer than 20 total observations, six consecutive points on one side of the median constitute a nonrandom shift, whereas a trend requires sequential movement in one direction.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Brucellosis is a systemic zoonotic bacterial infection acquired through contact with infected animals or consumption of contaminated animal products, especially unpasteurized milk or cheese. Clinical illness is nonspecific but commonly includes fever, sweats, fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, weight loss, and focal organ involvement; osteoarticular symptoms and hepatosplenomegaly can occur. Exposure history is therefore central to recognizing the diagnosis, which requires laboratory confirmation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize brucellosis in a patient with prolonged systemic febrile illness and osteoarticular symptoms after consumption of unpasteurized dairy products or exposure to infected livestock.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Retinitis pigmentosa is a genetically heterogeneous group of inherited retinal dystrophies. In the typical rod-cone form, rod photoreceptors are preferentially affected early. Progressive rod dysfunction causes nyctalopia and peripheral visual-field loss; cone dysfunction develops later and can impair color and central vision. Retinal pigment epithelium becomes secondarily abnormal, and migrating pigment-containing cells contribute to the characteristic bone-spicule fundus appearance.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain why typical retinitis pigmentosa first causes night blindness and peripheral-field loss by linking the phenotype to preferential early degeneration of rod photoreceptors.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Octreotide is a somatostatin analogue that suppresses growth hormone secretion. Somatostatin receptors are G protein-coupled receptors that signal through inhibitory G proteins; a major downstream effect is inhibition of adenylyl cyclase with reduced intracellular cAMP. Somatostatin-receptor activation also reduces intracellular calcium and promotes other inhibitory signaling, collectively decreasing hormone secretion.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect somatostatin-receptor activation to Gi-mediated inhibition of adenylyl cyclase and reduced cAMP, explaining the inhibitory endocrine effect of octreotide in acromegaly.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTTP/MTP) transfers triglyceride and other neutral lipids to nascent apolipoprotein B within the endoplasmic reticulum. This step is required for assembly and secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins: chylomicrons from intestinal epithelial cells and VLDL from hepatocytes. Biallelic loss-of-function MTTP variants cause abetalipoproteinemia, with extremely low or absent apoB-containing lipoproteins, fat and fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption, acanthocytosis, and progressive neurologic/retinal complications if untreated.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect abetalipoproteinemia to loss of MTTP-mediated lipid transfer onto nascent apoB in the endoplasmic reticulum, preventing formation of chylomicrons and VLDL and causing fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis is a progressive fibrosing disorder associated with gadolinium-based contrast exposure in patients with markedly impaired renal function. Delayed elimination of gadolinium-based contrast in severe kidney disease is the key clinical risk context; the disorder produces symmetric hard or woody skin induration and may cause severe flexion contractures and disability.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize nephrogenic systemic fibrosis as the characteristic diagnosis in a patient with severe renal impairment who develops symmetric woody skin induration and flexion contractures after gadolinium-based contrast exposure.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Bartonella henselae can be transmitted after a cat scratch, particularly from a kitten. Typical cat-scratch disease causes a papule or pustule at the inoculation site followed by enlarged, tender regional lymph nodes and often a low-grade fever.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize cat-scratch disease as the most likely diagnosis when a child develops a papule at a kitten-scratch site followed within several weeks by low-grade fever and tender regional lymphadenopathy.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Progressive supranuclear palsy is an atypical parkinsonian neurodegenerative tauopathy. Pathology includes predominantly 4-repeat tau accumulation in neurons and glia with degeneration involving basal ganglia and brainstem/oculomotor structures. The classic clinical phenotype combines early postural instability with backward falls, axial-predominant rigidity, and supranuclear impairment of vertical eye movements.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize progressive supranuclear palsy in an older adult with early backward falls, axial rigidity, poor levodopa response, and vertical supranuclear gaze impairment.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: In ALCAPA, the left coronary artery originates from the pulmonary artery rather than the aorta. Early after birth, relatively high pulmonary artery pressure can maintain some antegrade perfusion through the anomalous vessel. As pulmonary vascular resistance and pulmonary artery pressure fall, left-coronary perfusion pressure decreases and flow can reverse toward the low-pressure pulmonary artery; collateral flow from the right coronary system is then partly lost into the pulmonary artery (coronary steal), producing left-ventricular myocardial ischemia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain why infants with ALCAPA often become symptomatic after an initially well neonatal period: falling pulmonary vascular resistance and pulmonary artery pressure reduce antegrade left-coronary perfusion and promote retrograde coronary steal into the pulmonary artery.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A pulmonary arteriovenous malformation directly connects a branch of the pulmonary arterial circulation with the pulmonary venous circulation, allowing a fraction of deoxygenated venous blood to bypass ventilated alveoli and the pulmonary capillary gas-exchange interface. This anatomic right-to-left shunt raises the alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient and produces hypoxemia that improves poorly even when inspired oxygen concentration is markedly increased because the shunted blood never contacts alveolar gas.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain why a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation causes oxygen-resistant hypoxemia: deoxygenated blood bypasses ventilated alveoli through an anatomic right-to-left intrapulmonary shunt and mixes with oxygenated blood.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: MC2R is the adrenal ACTH receptor and signals predominantly through Gs to adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and protein kinase A in zona fasciculata cells to promote cortisol steroidogenesis. Loss of MC2R function therefore produces ACTH resistance with low cortisol and compensatory high ACTH. Mineralocorticoid secretion is classically preserved because aldosterone production in the zona glomerulosa is regulated primarily by angiotensin II and extracellular potassium through calcium-dependent signaling rather than by ACTH.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain the isolated glucocorticoid deficiency of MC2R-mediated familial glucocorticoid deficiency: ACTH-Gs-cAMP signaling fails in zona fasciculata while angiotensin II/potassium control of zona glomerulosa preserves aldosterone secretion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: FOXP3 is a transcription factor required for the development and suppressive function of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells. Loss of FOXP3 function impairs peripheral immune tolerance, permitting widespread autoreactive lymphocyte activity and early-onset autoimmune enteropathy, endocrinopathy, and dermatitis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect FOXP3 loss in IPEX syndrome to defective regulatory T-cell function and failure of peripheral immune tolerance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NMOSD is an autoimmune astrocytopathy strongly associated with IgG antibodies against aquaporin-4, a water channel enriched on astrocytic endfeet in the optic nerves, spinal cord, and area postrema. Attacks commonly manifest as optic neuritis, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and area postrema syndrome.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize NMOSD from the optic-spinal-area-postrema pattern, especially longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Staphylococcus aureus exfoliative toxins A and B are serine proteases that selectively cleave desmoglein-1, disrupting desmosomal adhesion in the superficial epidermis at the stratum granulosum. Desmoglein-3 is spared, helping explain mucosal sparing.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain SSSS as exfoliative-toxin-mediated cleavage of desmoglein-1 in the superficial epidermis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: LAM is characterized by abnormal proliferation of smooth-muscle-like LAM cells in lung parenchyma, airways, blood vessels, and lymphatics, producing diffuse cystic lung destruction. Dysregulation of TSC1/TSC2-mTOR signaling is central, and renal angiomyolipomas are a characteristic extrapulmonary association.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize lymphangioleiomyomatosis from diffuse thin-walled pulmonary cysts, recurrent pneumothorax, female sex, and renal angiomyolipoma.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: After prolonged starvation, rapid carbohydrate delivery raises insulin. Insulin drives phosphate and potassium into cells while anabolic pathways consume phosphate for phosphorylated intermediates and ATP. Depleted total-body stores make the fall in serum phosphate particularly dangerous, causing muscle weakness, respiratory failure, arrhythmias, and neurologic dysfunction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain refeeding syndrome as an insulin-driven intracellular shift and utilization of phosphate and other electrolytes after carbohydrate reintroduction in a severely malnourished patient.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Typical AVNRT requires dual AV nodal pathways: a fast pathway with rapid conduction and a relatively long refractory period, and a slow pathway with slower conduction and a shorter refractory period. A premature atrial impulse can encounter a refractory fast pathway, travel antegrade down the recovered slow pathway, then return retrograde through the now-recovered fast pathway to establish a reentrant circuit.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain typical slow-fast AVNRT using the different conduction velocities and refractory periods of dual AV nodal pathways.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Microscopic colitis produces chronic watery nonbloody diarrhea despite a grossly normal or near-normal colonoscopy. Collagenous colitis is defined histologically by a thickened subepithelial collagen band with inflammatory cells in the lamina propria; lymphocytic colitis instead has prominent intraepithelial lymphocytosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize collagenous microscopic colitis from chronic watery nonbloody diarrhea, normal colonoscopy, and a thickened subepithelial collagen band on biopsy.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: In a noninferiority trial, the confidence interval for the prespecified treatment-effect contrast is compared with a clinically justified noninferiority margin. If the entire confidence interval excludes the region worse than the margin, noninferiority is demonstrated. Superiority generally requires the confidence interval also to exclude the null value in the favorable direction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Interpret a noninferiority trial by comparing the full confidence interval with the prespecified noninferiority margin and separately evaluating whether superiority is supported.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Post-transfusion purpura is a rare alloimmune transfusion reaction in previously sensitized individuals, often multiparous women. Platelet-specific alloantibodies develop or rebound after exposure to platelet antigens in transfused blood products and cause abrupt, severe thrombocytopenia, classically several days after transfusion.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize post-transfusion purpura as severe delayed alloimmune thrombocytopenia occurring several days after transfusion, especially in a previously sensitized multiparous patient.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Bilateral injury to the ventral pons interrupts corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts, causing quadriplegia and anarthria. The dorsal pontine tegmentum and ascending reticular activating system are spared, preserving consciousness; vertical eye movements and blinking can also remain intact because their principal control structures are rostral to the ventral pontine lesion.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Localize locked-in syndrome to bilateral ventral pontine corticospinal/corticobulbar injury with preservation of dorsal arousal pathways and vertical eye movements.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ABCA12 is an ATP-binding cassette lipid transporter in epidermal keratinocytes that is critical for lamellar-granule lipid delivery to the stratum corneum. Severe loss of ABCA12 function disrupts lipid transport and extracellular lipid-barrier formation, producing marked hyperkeratosis and a profoundly impaired epidermal barrier.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain harlequin ichthyosis as an ABCA12-mediated defect of keratinocyte lamellar-granule lipid transport that disrupts the stratum-corneum lipid barrier.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CTNS encodes cystinosin, a lysosomal membrane transporter that moves cystine from the lysosomal lumen into the cytoplasm. Loss of cystinosin causes lysosomal cystine accumulation and crystal formation in many tissues; proximal tubular cell dysfunction produces generalized Fanconi syndrome.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain nephropathic cystinosis as a CTNS/cystinosin defect that prevents lysosomal cystine export, causing cystine accumulation and renal Fanconi syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Congenital afibrinogenemia is a severe quantitative fibrinogen disorder, usually autosomal recessive, caused by pathogenic variants affecting fibrinogen-chain genes or fibrinogen synthesis/assembly/secretion. Near-absence of circulating fibrinogen prevents normal fibrin clot formation, causing marked prolongation of fibrin-dependent clotting assays.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize congenital afibrinogenemia from early bleeding plus absent functional and antigenic fibrinogen with marked prolongation of fibrin-dependent coagulation assays.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Rotor syndrome results from combined loss of the sinusoidal organic anion transporters OATP1B1 and OATP1B3, encoded by SLCO1B1 and SLCO1B3. Impaired hepatic uptake/reuptake of conjugated bilirubin from sinusoidal blood reduces hepatic storage and promotes predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinemia without the dark hepatic pigment of Dubin-Johnson syndrome.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain Rotor syndrome as loss of OATP1B1/OATP1B3-mediated sinusoidal hepatic uptake/reuptake of conjugated bilirubin.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Systemic mastocytosis is a clonal mast-cell neoplasm commonly driven by an activating KIT mutation, most often KIT D816V. Constitutive KIT receptor-tyrosine-kinase signaling permits stem-cell-factor-independent mast-cell survival and proliferation; mediator release and tissue infiltration produce multisystem symptoms.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain systemic mastocytosis as a clonal mast-cell disorder driven most commonly by constitutive KIT D816V receptor-tyrosine-kinase signaling.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Compression or injury of the rostral dorsal midbrain/pretectal region near the superior colliculus disrupts vertical gaze circuitry and pretectal pupillary pathways. The characteristic syndrome includes impaired conjugate upgaze, convergence-retraction nystagmus, and pupillary light-near dissociation; pineal-region masses are a classic cause.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Parinaud syndrome from a dorsal midbrain lesion causing impaired upgaze, convergence-retraction nystagmus, and light-near dissociation.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: POR transfers electrons from NADPH to microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes in the endoplasmic reticulum, including CYP17A1, CYP21A2, and CYP19A1. Loss of POR therefore produces a combined steroidogenic defect rather than deficiency of a single adrenal enzyme.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain P450 oxidoreductase deficiency as failure of NADPH-dependent electron transfer to multiple microsomal steroidogenic cytochrome P450 enzymes.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Efficient patient-centered agenda setting first elicits the patient's complete list of concerns before detailed exploration, then collaboratively prioritizes which concerns can be addressed during the current visit and plans follow-up for remaining issues.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use patient-centered agenda setting by eliciting all concerns early and collaboratively prioritizing them before detailed evaluation.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: HSD3B2 converts Δ5 steroids to Δ4 steroids in adrenal cortex and gonads: pregnenolone to progesterone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone to 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and DHEA to androstenedione. Deficiency reduces glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, and gonadal sex-steroid synthesis and raises Δ5 precursors.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize HSD3B2 deficiency from accumulation of Δ5 steroids and identify the shared Δ5-to-Δ4 steroid conversion catalyzed by 3β-HSD2.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A deliberate period of attentive silence can communicate presence, avoid interrupting emotional processing, and give the patient time to reflect or continue speaking; it is especially appropriate immediately after an emotionally intense disclosure or while a patient is crying.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use attentive therapeutic silence rather than interruption, false reassurance, or premature task-focused questioning during acute emotional processing.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pendrin, encoded by SLC26A4, functions as an apical anion exchanger in thyroid and inner-ear epithelia. In thyroid follicular cells, loss of pendrin reduces iodide efflux into the follicular lumen and impairs iodide organification; inner-ear dysfunction causes sensorineural hearing loss and enlarged vestibular aqueducts.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain Pendred syndrome as loss of SLC26A4/pendrin-mediated apical anion transport, including reduced thyroid iodide efflux into the follicular lumen.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function variants in repolarizing potassium channels can increase outward potassium current during the ventricular action potential, abbreviating action-potential duration and the effective refractory period. This promotes reentry and predisposes to atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden death.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain how gain-of-function repolarizing potassium-channel variants cause short QT syndrome by shortening action-potential duration and refractory period.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Cathepsin K is a lysosomal cysteine protease highly expressed in osteoclasts that degrades type I and II collagen and other bone-matrix proteins in the acidic resorption compartment. CTSK loss impairs organic bone-matrix degradation, increasing bone density while making bone brittle.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain pycnodysostosis as impaired cathepsin-K-mediated degradation of collagenous bone matrix by otherwise present osteoclasts.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GNPTAB encodes the alpha/beta subunits of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase, which initiates mannose-6-phosphate targeting of lysosomal hydrolases in the Golgi. Loss of this enzyme causes lysosomal enzymes to be missorted and secreted extracellularly rather than delivered efficiently to lysosomes.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain mucolipidosis II as GNPTAB-dependent failure of mannose-6-phosphate targeting of lysosomal enzymes in the Golgi.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ClC-5, encoded by CLCN5, is a chloride/proton exchanger localized to proximal-tubule endosomes. Loss of ClC-5 disrupts endosomal ion handling/acidification and receptor-mediated endocytosis of filtered low-molecular-weight proteins, producing low-molecular-weight proteinuria with hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive kidney disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain low-molecular-weight proteinuria in Dent disease as a consequence of CLCN5/ClC-5-dependent proximal-tubule endosomal dysfunction and impaired receptor-mediated endocytosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Clear communication minimizes medical jargon and acronyms, uses common everyday words, defines necessary medical terms in simple language, and prioritizes a small number of key messages so patients can understand and act on health information.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use plain-language communication by replacing jargon with common words and defining unavoidable medical terminology.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC16A2 encodes MCT8, a thyroid-hormone cell-membrane transporter important for T3 entry into neurons and across blood-brain-barrier endothelium. Loss of MCT8 reduces neuronal thyroid-hormone availability despite abnormal circulating thyroid-hormone concentrations.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain the neurologic phenotype of MCT8 deficiency as impaired thyroid-hormone transport into developing brain cells.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Interrupted time-series designs use repeated outcome measurements before and after an intervention. Segmented regression estimates the preintervention trend and tests whether the intervention is associated with an immediate level change, a change in postintervention slope, or both, helping distinguish an intervention effect from the preexisting secular trend.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Choose segmented interrupted time-series regression to evaluate a quality-improvement intervention when repeated pre/post measurements and a preexisting secular trend are present.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Barttin-dependent ClC-K channels in the stria vascularis are required for the ionic environment and endocochlear potential that drive auditory transduction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain sensorineural deafness in BSND-related Bartter syndrome through impaired strial ion transport.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC35C1 encodes the Golgi GDP-fucose transporter. Deficiency prevents normal fucosylation of leukocyte glycans, including sialyl-Lewis X selectin ligands, impairing selectin-mediated leukocyte rolling and extravasation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain LAD type II as defective GDP-fucose transport and selectin-ligand fucosylation causing impaired leukocyte rolling.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SSPE is a delayed progressive CNS complication of persistent measles virus infection. Years after primary measles, patients develop behavioral or cognitive decline followed by myoclonus, motor deterioration, and characteristic periodic EEG abnormalities; elevated measles antibody in CSF supports the diagnosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize SSPE from delayed progressive neurocognitive decline and myoclonus after measles infection with characteristic EEG and CSF findings.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Carbonic anhydrase II catalyzes rapid interconversion of carbon dioxide and water with carbonic acid/bicarbonate and protons. Loss of CA2 impairs osteoclast generation of protons needed for bone resorption and disrupts renal acid-base handling, producing osteopetrosis together with renal tubular acidosis and cerebral calcification.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain osteopetrosis in carbonic anhydrase II deficiency as impaired osteoclast proton generation and resorption-lacuna acidification.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Calsequestrin-2, encoded by CASQ2, is a high-capacity calcium-binding protein in the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum that helps buffer luminal calcium and regulate ryanodine-receptor release. Loss of CASQ2 destabilizes calcium storage/release during adrenergic stress, promoting spontaneous diastolic calcium release, delayed afterdepolarizations, and triggered ventricular arrhythmias.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain CASQ2-related CPVT as abnormal sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium storage/release causing catecholamine-triggered delayed afterdepolarizations.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CYP7A1 encodes cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase, which catalyzes the initial and rate-controlling step of the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway from cholesterol. Loss of CYP7A1 reduces bile-acid production and cholesterol catabolism, promoting hepatic cholesterol accumulation, increased LDL cholesterol, and gallstone/atherosclerotic risk.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify CYP7A1 as the enzyme initiating the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway by 7alpha-hydroxylating cholesterol.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Aromatase, encoded by CYP19A1, converts androgens to estrogens. Gain-of-function regulatory rearrangements or overexpression increase extragonadal aromatase activity, producing estrogen excess with pre- or peripubertal gynecomastia, accelerated bone maturation, and sometimes reduced adult height.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain aromatase excess syndrome as CYP19A1 overexpression causing increased peripheral conversion of androgens to estrogens.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ABCG5 and ABCG8 form an ATP-binding cassette sterol-export heterodimer in intestinal enterocytes and hepatocytes. Loss of function reduces efflux of plant sterols back into the intestinal lumen and into bile, increasing dietary plant-sterol absorption and reducing biliary excretion, with systemic sterol accumulation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain sitosterolemia as ABCG5/ABCG8 failure of intestinal and hepatobiliary sterol efflux.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: When weight is relevant but potentially stigmatizing, a patient-centered opening asks permission before discussing it and uses nonjudgmental, person-centered language. This supports autonomy, reduces unsolicited weight-focused counseling, and permits the patient to decline or defer the topic.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use permission-based, nonstigmatizing communication when initiating a clinically relevant discussion about weight.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: KCNJ10 encodes the inward-rectifier potassium channel Kir4.1. In the distal convoluted tubule, basolateral Kir4.1-dependent potassium conductance is required for normal epithelial electrical and potassium-sensing physiology that supports sodium-chloride reabsorption. Loss of Kir4.1 produces a salt-wasting tubulopathy with hypokalemia and accompanies the neurologic and auditory phenotype of EAST/SeSAME syndrome.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link KCNJ10 loss in EAST/SeSAME syndrome to impaired basolateral Kir4.1 potassium conductance in the distal convoluted tubule.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: EXT1 and EXT2 form a heparan-sulfate polymerase complex. Loss of EXT function impairs heparan-sulfate chain synthesis and perturbs signaling in growth-plate chondrocytes, predisposing to multiple cartilage-capped osteochondromas.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify impaired heparan-sulfate polymerization as the core molecular defect in EXT1/EXT2-related hereditary multiple osteochondromas.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ABCA1 transfers cellular cholesterol and phospholipids to apolipoprotein A-I, initiating nascent HDL formation and promoting cholesterol efflux from macrophages and other cells. Biallelic ABCA1 loss markedly lowers HDL and causes cholesteryl-ester accumulation in reticuloendothelial tissues.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link Tangier disease to failure of ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux onto apo A-I and impaired nascent HDL formation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Immortal time bias occurs when a period during which an outcome could not have occurred for a participant to be classified as exposed is incorrectly assigned to the exposed group. The guaranteed survival interval before exposure can create a spurious protective association unless exposure is modeled as time-varying or person-time is classified correctly.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize immortal time bias when guaranteed survival before treatment initiation is incorrectly credited to the treated group in an observational cohort.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Alexander disease is an astrocytopathy caused predominantly by heterozygous gain-of-function variants in GFAP. Abnormal GFAP accumulation and astrocytic stress are associated with Rosenthal fibers and characteristic white-matter disease, often with frontal predominance in early-onset disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Diagnose Alexander disease from its early neurologic phenotype, frontal-predominant white-matter involvement, and pathogenic GFAP variant.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: TBX5 encodes a T-box transcription factor required for coordinated development of the upper limbs and heart. Haploinsufficiency disrupts radial-ray development and cardiac septation/conduction, producing the characteristic heart-hand phenotype.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify TBX5 as the developmental transcription factor linking radial-ray abnormalities with cardiac septation and conduction disease in Holt-Oram syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of the mesenteric fat pad after substantial weight loss can narrow the aortomesenteric angle, compressing the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery anteriorly and the aorta posteriorly and causing proximal obstruction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize superior mesenteric artery syndrome as acquired compression of the third duodenal portion between the SMA and aorta after major weight loss.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CIITA and the RFX complex are transcriptional regulators required for MHC class II gene expression. Loss of CIITA can abolish MHC II expression on antigen-presenting cells, impairing positive selection and peripheral activation of CD4-positive T cells and causing combined immunodeficiency.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain bare lymphocyte syndrome type II as failure of transcriptional regulation of MHC class II expression, causing defective CD4 T-cell selection and antigen presentation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NR5A1 encodes steroidogenic factor 1 (SF-1), a nuclear receptor transcription factor that regulates genes required for gonadal development, steroidogenesis, and reproductive function. Pathogenic variants can cause 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis or undervirilization, often with preserved adrenal function.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify SF-1/NR5A1 as a transcriptional regulator of gonadal development and steroidogenic gene expression in 46,XY disorders of sex development.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Unequal crossover creates a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene in which ACTH-responsive CYP11B1 regulatory sequences drive CYP11B2 aldosterone-synthase coding sequences. Aldosterone synthase is therefore ectopically expressed in the zona fasciculata and aldosterone production becomes ACTH-dependent rather than primarily renin-angiotensin regulated.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism as ACTH-driven aldosterone-synthase expression from a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Severe renal microvascular injury and markedly reduced cortical perfusion, often in obstetric catastrophe, sepsis, or disseminated intravascular coagulation, can cause ischemic necrosis of renal cortical tissue with relative sparing of the medulla.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize renal cortical necrosis from persistent severe AKI/anuria after obstetric hemorrhage or DIC and characteristic cortical ischemic imaging.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Classic stiff-person syndrome is an autoimmune CNS disorder characterized by fluctuating axial and proximal-limb rigidity and painful spasms triggered by sensory or emotional stimuli; high-titer anti-GAD65 antibodies are common and reflect association with impaired inhibitory GABAergic neurotransmission.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Diagnose stiff-person syndrome from chronic axial/proximal rigidity, stimulus-triggered spasms, continuous motor activity, and anti-GAD65 autoimmunity.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SEC23B is a component of the COPII coat that mediates export of newly synthesized proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum toward the Golgi. Biallelic SEC23B defects impair erythroid maturation and protein trafficking/processing, causing congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II with ineffective erythropoiesis and characteristic binucleated erythroblasts.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link SEC23B-related congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II to defective COPII-mediated ER-to-Golgi protein transport.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: IKBKG encodes IKK-gamma/NEMO, the regulatory component of the IKK complex required for activation of NF-kappa-B. Loss of normal IKBKG function impairs NF-kappa-B-mediated survival signaling, increasing susceptibility to apoptosis and producing the X-linked dominant multisystem phenotype of incontinentia pigmenti.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify defective IKBKG/NEMO-dependent NF-kappa-B activation as the molecular basis of incontinentia pigmenti.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function NLRP3 variants cause excessive assembly/activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, increasing caspase-1-dependent maturation of proinflammatory cytokines, particularly IL-1 beta and IL-18. This produces the spectrum of cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link NLRP3 gain of function in CAPS to excessive inflammasome activation and increased caspase-1-mediated IL-1 beta maturation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: When a patient expresses anger, an effective first communication step is to recognize and reflect the emotion explicitly. Acknowledgment demonstrates that the clinician has heard the concern and creates space for clarification before explanation, defense, or problem solving.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use explicit acknowledgment/reflection as the first response to a patient's expressed anger before explanation or problem solving.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: TAFAZZIN encodes tafazzin, an inner-mitochondrial-membrane phospholipid transacylase required for remodeling immature cardiolipin into mature cardiolipin species. Defective cardiolipin remodeling disrupts mitochondrial membrane organization and respiratory-chain function, producing the X-linked Barth syndrome phenotype.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify defective mitochondrial cardiolipin remodeling by tafazzin as the molecular defect in Barth syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: HSD17B3 is expressed predominantly in the testes and catalyzes the NADPH-dependent conversion of androstenedione to testosterone. Loss of enzyme activity reduces testicular testosterone production and causes undervirilization in 46,XY individuals.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify androstenedione-to-testosterone conversion as the reaction catalyzed by testicular 17β-HSD3.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Surfactant protein B is essential for normal pulmonary surfactant organization and function, including intracellular packaging of surfactant components and formation/presentation of the phospholipid film at the alveolar air-liquid interface. Biallelic SFTPB loss can cause severe refractory neonatal respiratory failure even in term infants.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain severe neonatal respiratory failure in SFTPB deficiency as failure of normal pulmonary surfactant organization and alveolar phospholipid-film function.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic UMOD variants impair uromodulin folding and cause abnormal uromodulin accumulation in the endoplasmic reticulum of thick ascending limb cells, producing a renal-limited endoplasmic-reticulum storage disease and progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain ADTKD-UMOD as a thick-ascending-limb endoplasmic-reticulum storage disease caused by abnormal uromodulin folding and retention.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function PIEZO1 variants slow inactivation or facilitate opening of the mechanically activated cation channel, increasing erythrocyte cation permeability and disrupting red-cell ion/volume homeostasis, which produces cellular dehydration and chronic hemolysis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate PIEZO1 gain-of-function and slowed mechanosensitive-channel inactivation to increased erythrocyte cation permeability and hereditary xerocytosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Insufficient GLUT1-mediated glucose transport across the blood-brain barrier causes cerebral energy deficiency and hypoglycorrhachia despite a normal blood glucose concentration.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize GLUT1 deficiency syndrome from neurologic dysfunction plus low CSF glucose despite normal blood glucose.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ABCC6 deficiency is associated with low circulating inorganic pyrophosphate, reducing an important inhibitor of mineralization and permitting ectopic calcification of elastic tissues in skin, retina, and blood vessels.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect ABCC6 deficiency in pseudoxanthoma elasticum with reduced inorganic pyrophosphate and ectopic elastic-tissue mineralization.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: KCNJ2 encodes Kir2.1, an inward-rectifier potassium channel important for setting and stabilizing skeletal/cardiac resting membrane potential and for terminal cardiac repolarization. Pathogenic variants can exert dominant-negative effects that reduce Kir2.1 current.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify Kir2.1/KCNJ2 as an inward-rectifier potassium channel that stabilizes muscle resting membrane potential and terminal cardiac repolarization.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of the intestinal SLC26A3 chloride-bicarbonate exchanger impairs chloride absorption and bicarbonate secretion in ileum/colon, causing chloride-rich watery diarrhea, extracellular-volume depletion, hypochloremia, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize congenital chloride diarrhea from neonatal chloride-rich watery diarrhea, low urinary chloride, and hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Reduced glucocorticoid-receptor signaling weakens cortisol-mediated negative feedback at the hypothalamus and pituitary, increasing CRH/ACTH drive and cortisol production. ACTH also increases adrenal mineralocorticoid-active steroids and androgens, producing hypertension/hypokalemia and hyperandrogenic manifestations without classic Cushingoid features.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain primary generalized glucocorticoid resistance as impaired glucocorticoid-receptor feedback causing compensatory CRH/ACTH activation and hypercortisolism without Cushingoid features.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: INSR encodes the insulin receptor, a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase. Severe loss of insulin-receptor function causes profound insulin resistance with hyperinsulinemia, fasting hypoglycemia/postprandial hyperglycemia, growth restriction, and characteristic somatic findings.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify the insulin receptor as a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase and connect severe biallelic INSR dysfunction with Donohue syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NOD2 is a cytosolic pattern-recognition receptor whose canonical bacterial ligand is muramyl dipeptide, a peptidoglycan component. Pathogenic NOD2 variants cause Blau syndrome, an early-onset granulomatous autoinflammatory syndrome affecting skin, joints, and eyes.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify muramyl dipeptide as the canonical bacterial ligand sensed by the intracellular NOD2 receptor implicated in Blau syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Effective error disclosure explicitly acknowledges the error and its known consequences, communicates what is known without speculation, explains how harm will be mitigated and recurrences prevented, accepts appropriate responsibility, and includes a sincere apology.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use transparent, timely, nondefensive communication when disclosing a confirmed harmful medical error, including known facts, apology, mitigation, and planned follow-up without speculation or blame.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency prevents normal cleavage of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers, allowing highly platelet-adhesive VWF multimers to accumulate on endothelium and form platelet-rich microthrombi that cause thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, and ischemic organ dysfunction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain TTP as severe ADAMTS13 deficiency causing persistence of ultra-large VWF multimers and platelet-rich microvascular thrombosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic IgG antibodies against the NR1 subunit of the NMDA receptor cause receptor internalization and reduced NMDA-receptor-mediated synaptic signaling; young women commonly develop prominent psychiatric symptoms followed by seizures, movement disorders, and autonomic instability, with an association with ovarian teratoma.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis from the characteristic psychiatric, seizure, movement-disorder, and autonomic syndrome, particularly in a young woman with ovarian teratoma.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity from pathogenic ALPL variants prevents normal hydrolysis of inorganic pyrophosphate, allowing extracellular pyrophosphate to accumulate and inhibit hydroxyapatite crystal growth and bone/tooth mineralization.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect ALPL/tissue-nonspecific alkaline-phosphatase deficiency with inorganic pyrophosphate accumulation and impaired hydroxyapatite mineralization in hypophosphatasia.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A nonselective beta blocker, preferably nadolol, is first-line therapy for catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Select a nonselective beta blocker as first-line chronic therapy for CPVT.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants affecting the ENaC PY motif impair binding of the Nedd4-2 ubiquitin ligase and reduce channel ubiquitination/removal from the apical membrane, increasing ENaC abundance and distal sodium reabsorption. Volume expansion suppresses renin and aldosterone while potassium and hydrogen ion losses cause hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate Liddle syndrome to impaired Nedd4-2/ENaC interaction, reduced ENaC degradation, and low-renin low-aldosterone hypertension.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic SI variants reduce brush-border sucrase-isomaltase activity, impairing digestion of sucrose and portions of starch and producing osmotic gastrointestinal symptoms after exposure to these carbohydrates.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize congenital sucrase-isomaltase deficiency from carbohydrate-triggered diarrhea with preserved villous architecture and selective low sucrase/isomaltase activity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Heterozygous loss-of-function CASR variants raise the extracellular-calcium set point required to suppress parathyroid hormone secretion and increase renal tubular calcium reabsorption, producing mild lifelong hypercalcemia with inappropriately normal or mildly elevated PTH and relative hypocalciuria.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain FHH type 1 as CaSR loss of function that raises the calcium set point for PTH suppression and increases renal calcium reabsorption.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ATP7A encodes a P-type copper-transporting ATPase that transports copper across cellular membranes and is essential for intestinal copper absorption and tissue copper distribution. Severe ATP7A loss of function produces systemic copper deficiency and reduced activity of multiple copper-dependent enzymes.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify Menkes disease as an ATP7A-mediated copper-transport defect causing impaired copper absorption/distribution and systemic copper-enzyme deficiency.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Confounding by indication occurs when the clinical factors prompting a treatment also predict the outcome, distorting an observational treatment-outcome association.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize confounding by indication when the clinical reason for assigning a treatment is also a determinant of the measured outcome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Teach-back checks the clarity of clinician communication by asking the patient to explain in their own words what they need to know or do; it is framed as a test of the clinician's explanation rather than a test of the patient's memory and should be repeated after clarification if misunderstanding is identified.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use teach-back to verify comprehension by asking patients to explain care instructions in their own words rather than relying on yes/no confirmation or passive written materials.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A somatic PIGA mutation in a hematopoietic stem cell impairs glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor biosynthesis, causing loss of GPI-anchored complement regulators such as CD55 and CD59 and thereby permitting complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and thrombosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain PNH as an acquired somatic PIGA defect causing loss of GPI-anchored CD55/CD59 and complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: MELAS is a mitochondrial disorder, most often related to pathogenic mitochondrial DNA variants such as MT-TL1 m.3243A>G, in which impaired oxidative phosphorylation causes lactic acidemia and recurrent neurologic stroke-like episodes whose lesions do not respect arterial vascular territories.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize MELAS from lactic acidemia, maternal inheritance, seizures, and stroke-like MRI lesions that cross arterial territories.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PHEX loss of function increases FGF23 activity. Excess FGF23 reduces proximal-tubular phosphate reabsorption by promoting internalization of sodium-phosphate cotransporters and also lowers calcitriol synthesis, producing chronic phosphate wasting and defective bone mineralization.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect PHEX deficiency with excess FGF23 and proximal-tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporter internalization in X-linked hypophosphatemia.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PKP2 encodes plakophilin-2, a desmosomal component of cardiomyocyte intercalated-disc junctions. Pathogenic PKP2 variants impair desmosomal integrity and mechanical coupling, contributing to ventricular arrhythmias and progressive fibrofatty myocardial replacement.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify PKP2/plakophilin-2 as a cardiac desmosomal junction protein implicated in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Inherited defects in motile-cilia structure, function, or biogenesis impair mucociliary clearance. Many affected individuals have dynein-arm or other axonemal defects, causing chronic sinopulmonary disease; abnormal embryonic nodal cilia can randomize left-right patterning, and flagellar dysfunction can impair fertility.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize primary ciliary dyskinesia from chronic childhood otosinopulmonary disease, bronchiectasis, very low nasal nitric oxide, and situs inversus.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is required in enterocytes and hepatocytes for assembly and secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins. MTTP deficiency prevents formation/secretion of chylomicrons and VLDL, producing severe hypolipidemia, fat malabsorption, and fat-soluble-vitamin deficiency.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain abetalipoproteinemia as MTTP deficiency causing failure of apoB-containing chylomicron and VLDL assembly/secretion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CYP17A1 deficiency impairs cortisol and sex-steroid synthesis. Elevated ACTH diverts steroid precursors toward mineralocorticoid-active 11-deoxycorticosterone and corticosterone, causing hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis while androgen deficiency causes absent or delayed sexual development.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify excess 11-deoxycorticosterone as the mineralocorticoid-active steroid driving hypertension in 17α-hydroxylase deficiency.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: After prolonged starvation, carbohydrate refeeding causes an insulin surge that drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells while total-body stores are depleted. The resulting hypophosphatemia can impair ATP generation, cardiac conduction, and respiratory-muscle function.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain refeeding hypophosphatemia as insulin-driven intracellular phosphate uptake occurring on a background of depleted total-body phosphate.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Verification bias occurs when receipt of the reference-standard test depends on the index-test result or related clinical suspicion, so disease status is not verified comparably across index-test groups and calculated diagnostic accuracy becomes biased.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize verification bias when the probability of receiving the diagnostic reference standard depends on the index-test result or clinical suspicion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: For clinically important communication with a patient who has limited English proficiency, a qualified medical interpreter improves accuracy, privacy, informed decision-making, and patient safety; ad hoc interpretation by family members should not substitute for professional language assistance.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use a qualified medical interpreter—not an ad hoc family interpreter—for complex clinical communication with a patient who has limited English proficiency.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Normal aging is associated with progressive stiffening and reduced compliance of large arteries. Earlier return of reflected pressure waves augments systolic pressure, while reduced elastic recoil contributes to a wider pulse pressure and less effective buffering of abrupt hemodynamic changes.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate normal aging to reduced large-artery compliance and a wider pulse pressure.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SERPING1-related C1-inhibitor deficiency or dysfunction permits excessive kallikrein/contact-system activity and overproduction of bradykinin, causing episodic nonurticarial edema of skin, bowel, and upper airway.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize hereditary angioedema from recurrent nonurticarial edema, abdominal attacks, familial clustering, low C4, and reduced C1-inhibitor function.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Arylsulfatase A deficiency impairs lysosomal degradation of sulfatides, causing sulfatide accumulation in the central and peripheral nervous systems with progressive demyelination and neurodegeneration.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect arylsulfatase A deficiency with lysosomal sulfatide accumulation in metachromatic leukodystrophy.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic COL3A1 variants alter type III procollagen, an important structural component of skin, blood vessels, and hollow organs, causing tissue fragility and predisposition to spontaneous arterial or organ rupture.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify type III collagen as the COL3A1-encoded structural protein affected in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: LDLR loss of function reduces hepatic clearance of circulating LDL particles. LDL receptors normally bind apoB-100-containing LDL and mediate receptor-dependent uptake, so impaired receptor function causes marked lifelong elevation of LDL cholesterol and premature atherosclerosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate LDLR loss of function in familial hypercholesterolemia to reduced receptor-mediated hepatic clearance of circulating LDL.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: AVPR2 encodes the basolateral vasopressin V2 receptor in collecting-duct principal cells. Normal V2-receptor activation stimulates Gs, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and PKA, leading to apical insertion of AQP2 water channels; AVPR2 loss of function disrupts this pathway and prevents urinary concentration.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain X-linked nephrogenic diabetes insipidus as AVPR2 loss causing failure of Gs-cAMP-PKA-mediated apical AQP2 insertion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ATP7B is a P-type copper-transporting ATPase in hepatocytes that incorporates copper into ceruloplasmin and transports excess copper into bile. Loss of ATP7B function impairs biliary copper excretion, causing hepatic and extrahepatic copper accumulation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify ATP7B as the hepatocyte copper transporter required for ceruloplasmin incorporation and biliary copper excretion in Wilson disease.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of Gsα expression/function from GNAS abnormalities impairs receptor-coupled cAMP signaling in PTH target tissues. Renal PTH resistance reduces phosphaturia and calcitriol production, producing hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and elevated PTH; some forms also have Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize pseudohypoparathyroidism as GNAS/Gsα-mediated hormone resistance causing hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, elevated PTH, and Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic GAA loss of function causes deficiency of lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase, preventing normal lysosomal glycogen degradation. Glycogen accumulates within lysosomes, damaging cardiac and skeletal muscle.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize infantile Pompe disease from hypotonia and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with deficient lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase activity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Attrition bias is a selection bias that arises when losses to follow-up differ systematically between comparison groups or are related to prognosis/outcome, so the participants remaining for analysis are no longer comparable to those originally enrolled.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize attrition bias when differential, outcome-related loss to follow-up changes the composition of comparison groups.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Removing the low-resistance placental circuit increases systemic vascular resistance and left ventricular afterload at birth.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish the systemic effect of cord clamping from the pulmonary effects of the first breaths.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Distal RTA results from impaired hydrogen-ion secretion by alpha-intercalated cells of the collecting duct, including inherited or acquired defects of apical H+-ATPase-dependent acid secretion. Urine remains inappropriately alkaline despite systemic metabolic acidosis, promoting hypocitraturia and calcium-phosphate nephrolithiasis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize type 1 distal RTA as impaired alpha-intercalated-cell hydrogen-ion secretion causing alkaline urine, hypokalemic normal-anion-gap acidosis, and nephrolithiasis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ITGB2 mutations cause deficiency of the beta-2 integrin subunit CD18, impairing leukocyte integrins such as LFA-1 and Mac-1. Neutrophils can roll but cannot undergo normal firm adhesion to endothelial ICAMs and subsequent recruitment into infected tissue.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link LAD-I/CD18 deficiency to failure of beta-2-integrin-mediated firm neutrophil adhesion to endothelial ICAMs.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Most Friedreich ataxia results from biallelic intronic GAA-repeat expansions that reduce FXN transcription and frataxin. Frataxin deficiency impairs mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, disrupts respiratory-chain and aconitase function, mislocalizes iron, and increases oxidative stress.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect FXN GAA-repeat expansion in Friedreich ataxia with reduced frataxin and impaired mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Carbonic anhydrase II generates intracellular hydrogen ions required for acidification of the osteoclast resorption lacuna. CA2 deficiency impairs osteoclast-mediated mineral dissolution and can also impair renal acidification, producing osteopetrosis with renal tubular acidosis and intracranial calcification.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain CA2-deficiency osteopetrosis as failure of osteoclast proton generation and acidification of the bone-resorption lacuna.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss-of-function SCN5A variants reduce availability of the cardiac Nav1.5 fast sodium current. Reduced inward sodium current impairs rapid phase-0 depolarization and conduction, contributing to characteristic right-precordial ST-segment patterns and vulnerability to ventricular fibrillation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate SCN5A-associated Brugada syndrome to reduced fast inward sodium current and impaired phase-0 cardiac depolarization.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: HFE dysfunction reduces hepatocyte hepcidin upregulation. Low hepcidin fails to induce ferroportin internalization/degradation, so ferroportin remains active on enterocytes and macrophages, increasing dietary iron absorption and iron release into plasma.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain HFE-related hemochromatosis as inadequate hepcidin activity with excessive ferroportin-mediated iron export and absorption.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CYP11B1 normally converts 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and 11-deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone. Deficiency lowers cortisol, increases ACTH and adrenal androgen production, and causes accumulation of mineralocorticoid-active 11-deoxycorticosterone, leading to hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed renin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify the blocked CYP11B1 reactions in 11β-hydroxylase deficiency and connect DOC accumulation with low-renin hypertension.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The Z alpha-1 antitrypsin variant misfolds and polymerizes within hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum, causing toxic intracellular accumulation and liver disease. Reduced secretion simultaneously lowers circulating AAT, permitting neutrophil-elastase-mediated alveolar destruction in the lung.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish the hepatic gain-of-function mechanism of PI*ZZ alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency—ER polymer accumulation—from the pulmonary loss-of-function mechanism.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Collider bias occurs when analysis conditions on, stratifies by, or selects participants according to a variable that is a common effect of both an exposure and an outcome (or their causes). Conditioning on the collider can induce a spurious association between otherwise independent variables.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize collider/Berkson bias when study selection conditions on a variable that is caused by both the exposure and the outcome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic autoantibodies bind the noncollagenous NC1 domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes, producing rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify the alpha-3-chain type IV collagen NC1 domain as the autoantigen in anti-GBM/Goodpasture disease.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Ankyrin links the spectrin-based erythrocyte membrane skeleton to transmembrane proteins such as band 3. Defective vertical membrane-cytoskeletal interactions cause progressive membrane loss, reduced surface-area-to-volume ratio, spherocyte formation, and splenic sequestration.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect ANK1-related hereditary spherocytosis with defective vertical linkage between the spectrin cytoskeleton and the red-cell membrane.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Autoantibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels reduce calcium entry into motor nerve terminals and decrease acetylcholine release. Repetitive activation can transiently increase calcium accumulation and improve strength.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome from proximal weakness, autonomic dysfunction, hyporeflexia, exercise facilitation, and small-cell lung carcinoma.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Constitutive gain-of-function signaling through FGFR3 inhibits proliferation and differentiation of growth-plate chondrocytes, impairing endochondral ossification while largely preserving intramembranous ossification.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain achondroplasia as constitutive FGFR3 activation that suppresses growth-plate chondrocyte proliferation and endochondral ossification.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Anterior/superior malalignment of the infundibular (outlet) septum produces a large malaligned ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta, and subpulmonary right-ventricular outflow obstruction; right-ventricular hypertrophy develops secondarily.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate the anatomy of tetralogy of Fallot to anterior/superior displacement of the infundibular septum.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Tissue transglutaminase deamidates selected glutamine residues in gluten peptides to glutamate, increasing their negative charge and affinity for disease-associated HLA-DQ2/DQ8 molecules. Presentation of these peptides to CD4+ T cells drives mucosal inflammation and villous injury.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain how tissue transglutaminase-mediated deamidation of gluten enhances HLA-DQ2/DQ8 presentation and T-cell activation in celiac disease.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: MEN2 is caused by heterozygous germline gain-of-function variants in RET, which encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase. Constitutive or dysregulated RET signaling promotes C-cell and adrenal medullary tumorigenesis; MEN2A also predisposes to parathyroid hyperplasia/adenoma.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize MEN2A as a germline RET receptor-tyrosine-kinase gain-of-function syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Cystathionine beta-synthase normally condenses homocysteine with serine to form cystathionine in the transsulfuration pathway. CBS deficiency causes accumulation of homocysteine and methionine, relative cysteine deficiency, connective-tissue abnormalities, ectopia lentis, and marked thromboembolic risk.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify the blocked homocysteine-to-cystathionine transsulfuration reaction in classic CBS-deficiency homocystinuria.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Intention-to-treat analysis preserves the prognostic balance created by randomization by analyzing participants according to their originally assigned treatment group, regardless of nonadherence, crossover, or treatment discontinuation. It estimates the effect of treatment assignment rather than efficacy among adherers.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Apply the intention-to-treat principle by retaining participants in their originally randomized groups despite crossover or nonadherence.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Medical decision-making capacity is decision-specific and requires the ability to understand relevant information, appreciate how it applies to one's situation, reason about options and consequences, and communicate a stable choice. A patient does not lose capacity merely because the decision is risky or differs from the clinician's recommendation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Respect informed refusal when a patient demonstrates understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and ability to communicate a stable choice.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of the apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb impairs sodium chloride reabsorption, reduces the lumen-positive potential that normally drives paracellular calcium reabsorption, activates renin-aldosterone signaling, and produces hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with hypercalciuria.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify NKCC2 loss in the thick ascending limb as the transport defect in type 1 Bartter syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Warm-reactive IgG binds erythrocyte surface antigens. Splenic macrophages recognize Fc-coated erythrocytes and partially phagocytose or remove them from the circulation, producing predominantly extravascular hemolysis and microspherocyte formation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain warm AIHA as predominantly splenic Fc-mediated extravascular destruction of IgG-coated erythrocytes.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: IgG1/IgG3 autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors can functionally block receptors, accelerate receptor internalization, and activate complement, reducing functional receptor density and damaging the postsynaptic membrane.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain AChR-positive myasthenia gravis as antibody-mediated postsynaptic receptor loss and complement injury.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Type I collagen is a heterotrimer of two alpha-1(I) and one alpha-2(I) chains with a Gly-X-Y repeating triple-helical region. Pathogenic variants can reduce type I collagen quantity or disrupt helix structure, producing bone fragility and characteristic extraskeletal connective-tissue manifestations.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify type I collagen as the COL1A1/COL1A2 product responsible for classic osteogenesis imperfecta.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: MYH7 encodes beta-cardiac myosin heavy chain, a thick-filament motor protein of the sarcomere. Pathogenic variants in MYH7 are a major autosomal-dominant cause of nonsyndromic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify beta-myosin heavy chain encoded by MYH7 as a sarcomere thick-filament protein in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Autoimmune hepatitis is an immune-mediated inflammatory liver disease associated with loss of immune tolerance. Typical findings include hepatocellular aminotransferase elevation, increased IgG, autoantibodies such as ANA or anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and plasma-cell-rich interface hepatitis after competing causes are excluded.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize autoimmune hepatitis from elevated IgG, characteristic autoantibodies, hepatocellular injury, and plasma-cell-rich interface hepatitis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Aldosterone excess promotes distal hydrogen-ion secretion, contributing to metabolic alkalosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect mineralocorticoid excess to enhanced distal hydrogen-ion secretion and metabolic alkalosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: OTC normally combines mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate with ornithine to form citrulline. OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia; accumulated mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate spills into cytosolic pyrimidine synthesis, increasing urinary orotic acid.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify the blocked ornithine-plus-carbamoyl-phosphate-to-citrulline reaction in OTC deficiency and relate it to hyperammonemia with orotic aciduria.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Number needed to treat is the reciprocal of the absolute risk reduction: NNT = 1 / (control event rate − treatment event rate), conventionally rounded up to the next whole patient when needed.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Calculate NNT as the reciprocal of absolute risk reduction.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Structured bad-news communication frameworks such as SPIKES emphasize assessing the patient's perspective, delivering information clearly, and responding to emotions with empathy before continuing with further information and planning.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Respond to a patient's distress after bad news with empathic acknowledgment before providing additional complex information.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function variants in epithelial sodium channel subunits increase apical ENaC activity in the distal nephron, increasing sodium reabsorption and potassium/hydrogen secretion despite suppressed renin and aldosterone.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize low-renin, low-aldosterone hypokalemic hypertension as Liddle syndrome caused by constitutively increased ENaC activity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Deficiency or dysfunction of the platelet GPIb-IX-V complex impairs von Willebrand factor-mediated platelet adhesion to damaged subendothelium and produces giant platelets with thrombocytopenia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate Bernard-Soulier syndrome from other platelet disorders by linking giant thrombocytopenic platelets to defective GPIb-IX-V–vWF adhesion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Botulinum neurotoxin light chains cleave SNARE proteins required for fusion of acetylcholine-containing vesicles with the presynaptic membrane, preventing acetylcholine release and causing descending flaccid paralysis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain botulism as a presynaptic SNARE-cleavage disorder that blocks acetylcholine release at cholinergic nerve terminals.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Skeletal-muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency prevents phosphorolytic release of glucose-1-phosphate from muscle glycogen during exercise, causing exercise intolerance and the characteristic second-wind phenomenon.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link McArdle disease to impaired skeletal-muscle glycogen phosphorylase and failure of glycogen-to-glucose-1-phosphate conversion during exercise.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of one functional ELN allele reduces elastin dosage in arterial walls, producing elastin arteriopathy with congenital narrowing that characteristically involves the supravalvular aorta.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Associate supravalvular aortic stenosis caused by ELN loss of function with reduced elastin in the arterial extracellular matrix.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is required to transfer lipid to nascent apolipoprotein B during assembly of chylomicrons and VLDL; MTTP loss prevents secretion of apoB-containing lipoproteins.
