construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize VIPoma from fasting-persistent secretory diarrhea, hypokalemia, bicarbonate loss, and hypochlorhydria and connect the syndrome to excessive VIP-cAMP signaling.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Autonomous aldosterone excess increases ENaC-mediated sodium entry in collecting-duct principal cells and enhances basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase activity, creating a lumen-negative potential that favors potassium secretion through ROMK. Aldosterone also promotes hydrogen secretion by alpha-intercalated cells, producing hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis while volume expansion suppresses renin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect autonomous aldosterone excess to ENaC-mediated collecting-duct sodium reabsorption, potassium wasting, metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed renin.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC3A1 and SLC7A9 encode the two subunits of an apical heteromeric transporter in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells and the small intestine. Loss of transporter function impairs reabsorption of cystine and dibasic amino acids; poorly soluble cystine precipitates in urine and forms recurrent stones.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify cystinuria as a proximal tubular cystine/dibasic-amino-acid transport defect caused by SLC3A1/SLC7A9 dysfunction.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Huntington disease is caused by expansion of a CAG repeat in HTT. Repeat length can increase across generations, and large expansions occur disproportionately during paternal transmission because the repeat is unstable during spermatogenesis; increasing repeat length is generally associated with earlier disease onset.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain paternal anticipation in Huntington disease as expansion of an unstable HTT CAG repeat during spermatogenesis.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Out-of-frame deletions or other truncating DMD variants disrupt the translational reading frame, producing severely truncated unstable dystrophin that is degraded. Loss of dystrophin destabilizes the sarcolemma during contraction, causing repeated myofiber injury, high CK, progressive weakness, and replacement by fat/connective tissue.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use the dystrophin reading-frame rule to distinguish severe Duchenne disease from milder Becker disease and connect absent dystrophin to sarcolemmal instability.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The vitelline duct normally connects the embryonic midgut to the yolk sac and involutes during early development. Incomplete obliteration can leave a true ileal diverticulum; ectopic gastric mucosa may secrete acid, ulcerating adjacent ileal mucosa and causing painless lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify Meckel diverticulum as a vitelline-duct remnant and connect ectopic gastric mucosa to painless pediatric gastrointestinal bleeding.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Vancomycin binds the terminal D-alanyl-D-alanine motif of peptidoglycan precursors and sterically impairs cell-wall polymerization/cross-linking. VanA resistance remodels the precursor terminus to D-Ala-D-Lac, markedly reducing vancomycin binding affinity and allowing peptidoglycan synthesis to continue.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect vancomycin's D-Ala-D-Ala target to VanA-mediated replacement with D-Ala-D-Lac and high-level enterococcal resistance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Randomization balances measured and unmeasured prognostic factors on average. Intention-to-treat analysis retains participants in the groups to which they were randomized regardless of nonadherence, crossover, or protocol deviations, thereby preserving the main protection against selection bias conferred by random assignment.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify intention-to-treat analysis as the preferred primary strategy for preserving randomization in trials with nonadherence or treatment crossover.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: An acquired factor VIII autoantibody produces a new bleeding diathesis with an isolated prolonged aPTT. Because the inhibitor acts on factor VIII supplied by normal plasma, an incubated 1:1 mixing study fails to correct the aPTT; factor VIII activity is reduced.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize acquired hemophilia A from new-onset bleeding, isolated aPTT prolongation, failure of an incubated mixing study to correct, and reduced factor VIII activity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants in desmosomal proteins such as plakophilin-2 impair mechanical coupling between cardiomyocytes. Progressive myocyte injury and fibrofatty replacement, especially in the right ventricle, create an arrhythmogenic substrate that can produce ventricular tachycardia with left bundle branch block morphology and epsilon waves.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect the classic electrical and structural features of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy to defects in desmosomal proteins such as plakophilin-2.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The Z alpha-1 antitrypsin variant misfolds and polymerizes within hepatocytes, preventing normal secretion. Intrahepatocytic accumulation causes liver injury through a toxic gain-of-function mechanism, whereas pulmonary emphysema primarily reflects loss of circulating antiprotease activity.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish the liver gain-of-function mechanism of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency from the pulmonary loss-of-function mechanism.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: In tissues such as the renal proximal tubule, Gs-alpha is preferentially expressed from the maternal GNAS allele. Maternal GNAS loss of function impairs receptor-coupled adenylyl cyclase signaling, producing resistance to PTH and other Gs-coupled hormones together with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A and apply genomic imprinting to distinguish maternal GNAS inactivation with hormone resistance from paternal GNAS inactivation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CYP11B1 deficiency blocks conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone. Reduced cortisol increases ACTH and drives androgen excess, while accumulated deoxycorticosterone has mineralocorticoid activity that causes sodium retention, hypertension, hypokalemia, and suppression of renin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency from other congenital adrenal hyperplasias by recognizing deoxycorticosterone-mediated low-renin hypertension with androgen excess.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: In a 46,XY individual with functioning testes, Sertoli-cell anti-Müllerian hormone causes regression of Müllerian structures, but absent androgen receptor signaling prevents masculinization of external genitalia and causes sparse pubic/axillary hair. Aromatization of testicular androgens permits normal breast development at puberty.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate complete androgen insensitivity syndrome from other causes of primary amenorrhea by integrating karyotype, Müllerian anatomy, testosterone level, breast development, and pubic hair.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: IgG antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels reduce calcium entry and acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction. Repeated activation temporarily increases presynaptic calcium, producing facilitation of strength and reflexes; autonomic dysfunction is common and the syndrome is strongly associated with small-cell lung cancer.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome and connect exercise facilitation and autonomic dysfunction to antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Vitamin C is required as a cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases in the rough endoplasmic reticulum. Deficient hydroxylation destabilizes collagen and weakens connective tissue, causing perifollicular hemorrhages, gingival bleeding, corkscrew hairs, and poor wound healing.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link the clinical findings of scurvy to impaired vitamin C-dependent hydroxylation of proline and lysine during intracellular collagen synthesis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Alcohol dehydrogenase oxidizes methanol toward toxic formic acid/formate. Formate accumulation produces a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and disrupts mitochondrial respiration; retinal and optic-nerve tissues are particularly vulnerable. Fomepizole limits toxicity by inhibiting alcohol dehydrogenase before toxic metabolites accumulate.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate toxic alcohol metabolites by recognizing formic acid/formate as the mediator of methanol-associated metabolic acidosis and visual injury.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Teach-back is a health-literacy communication method in which the clinician asks the patient or caregiver to explain the information or required actions in their own words. It tests the clarity of the clinician's explanation rather than relying on a yes/no assertion of understanding.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use teach-back rather than yes/no confirmation to verify patient understanding of medical instructions and reduce communication-related safety risk.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Cold-reactive IgM binds red-cell surface antigens at lower temperatures and efficiently activates the classical complement pathway. C3 fragments remain deposited on red cells and promote hemolysis; the direct antiglobulin test is characteristically complement-positive.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize cold agglutinin disease and connect its complement-positive hemolysis to cold-reactive IgM-mediated activation of the classical complement pathway.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: During diastole, an incompetent aortic valve permits blood to flow from the aorta back into the left ventricle, accelerating the decline in aortic diastolic pressure. Chronic volume loading increases left-ventricular end-diastolic volume and total left-ventricular stroke volume, which can increase systolic pressure; together these effects widen pulse pressure.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain the widened pulse pressure of chronic aortic regurgitation as the combination of increased left-ventricular stroke volume and rapid diastolic runoff into the left ventricle.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: HFE dysfunction impairs hepatocyte upregulation of hepcidin. Hepcidin normally binds ferroportin and promotes its internalization and degradation. Low hepcidin therefore leaves more active ferroportin on enterocytes and reticuloendothelial cells, increasing intestinal iron absorption and iron release into plasma.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect HFE-related hemochromatosis to low hepcidin and increased ferroportin activity, explaining excessive intestinal iron absorption and systemic iron overload.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: In 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, disrupted pharyngeal-apparatus development can cause thymic hypoplasia and parathyroid hypoplasia. The thymic epithelium derives from the third pharyngeal pouch, the inferior parathyroids from the third pouch, and the superior parathyroids from the fourth pouch. Hypoplastic thymic tissue impairs T-cell development, while parathyroid hypoplasia can cause hypocalcemia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect the T-cell deficiency and hypocalcemia of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome to abnormal development of third- and fourth-pharyngeal-pouch derivatives, while distinguishing these endodermal pouch derivatives from neural-crest contributions to conotruncal development.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A unilateral medial medullary lesion affects corticospinal fibers in the pyramid before their caudal decussation, the already-crossed dorsal-column fibers ascending in the medial lemniscus, and ipsilateral hypoglossal fascicles. This produces contralateral weakness, contralateral loss of vibration/proprioception, and ipsilateral tongue weakness.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Localize medial medullary syndrome by integrating corticospinal, medial lemniscal, and hypoglossal deficits and correctly assigning the lesion side.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Effective osteoclastic resorption requires formation of a sealed resorption lacuna and acidification of that compartment through proton generation and transport. Defects in osteoclast proton pumps, chloride channels, or carbonic anhydrase II impair acidification and mineral dissolution, producing abnormally dense but brittle bone and reduced marrow space.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect the dense-but-fragile bone, marrow failure, and cranial-nerve compression of osteopetrosis to defective osteoclast acidification and bone resorption.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GnRH-producing neurons originate in the developing olfactory region and migrate through the cribriform plate to the hypothalamus. Developmental failure of this migration causes GnRH deficiency and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism while associated olfactory-system defects cause anosmia or hyposmia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain the combined anosmia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism of Kallmann syndrome by failed embryologic migration of GnRH neurons from the olfactory region to the hypothalamus.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants in the X-linked GLA gene reduce lysosomal alpha-galactosidase A activity. Inadequate degradation of globotriaosylceramide and related glycosphingolipids causes progressive lysosomal accumulation in vascular, renal, cardiac, and neural tissues.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Fabry disease from its characteristic early phenotype and connect it to X-linked GLA deficiency and lysosomal globotriaosylceramide accumulation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Hypobaric hypoxia stimulates peripheral chemoreceptors and increases ventilation, lowering PaCO2 and causing respiratory alkalosis. Over the next several days the kidneys increase bicarbonate excretion, reducing the alkalemic constraint on ventilatory drive and permitting sustained hyperventilation as acclimatization progresses.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain high-altitude ventilatory acclimatization by linking hypoxia-induced respiratory alkalosis to compensatory renal bicarbonate excretion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The positive likelihood ratio compares the probability of a positive result among individuals with disease with the probability of a positive result among individuals without disease. It equals sensitivity divided by the false-positive rate, or sensitivity/(1-specificity), and unlike predictive values is not determined by disease prevalence.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Calculate and interpret the positive likelihood ratio as sensitivity divided by one minus specificity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: An acquired PIGA mutation impairs glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor synthesis, preventing complement-regulatory proteins such as CD55 and CD59 from attaching normally to blood-cell surfaces. Loss of these regulators permits complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis and contributes to thrombosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect Coombs-negative intravascular hemolysis, unusual-site thrombosis, and loss of CD55/CD59 to an acquired PIGA mutation that impairs GPI-anchor synthesis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants in sarcomere proteins such as beta-myosin heavy chain or myosin-binding protein C cause myocyte hypertrophy and disarray. Asymmetric septal hypertrophy can create dynamic left-ventricular outflow obstruction, which worsens when ventricular volume falls and the septum and mitral valve are brought closer together.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and connect its dynamic obstructive physiology to autosomal-dominant sarcomere-protein mutations.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ATP7B is a hepatocellular copper-transporting ATPase involved in incorporating copper into ceruloplasmin and exporting excess copper into bile. Loss of ATP7B function impairs both processes, causing hepatic copper accumulation and reduced circulating ceruloplasmin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect Wilson disease to ATP7B dysfunction that impairs biliary copper excretion and copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Reduced renin and aldosterone impair distal potassium and hydrogen handling, causing hyperkalemia. Hyperkalemia suppresses proximal-tubular ammoniagenesis, reducing urinary ammonium buffering and net acid excretion and producing a hyperchloremic normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain the metabolic acidosis of type 4 RTA by linking hypoaldosteronism-induced hyperkalemia to reduced renal ammoniagenesis and ammonium excretion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The lateral corticospinal tract has already crossed in the caudal medulla, so a spinal hemicord lesion causes ipsilateral weakness below the lesion. Dorsal-column fibers ascend ipsilaterally in the cord and cross in the medulla, so vibration/proprioception loss is also ipsilateral. Spinothalamic fibers cross within the spinal cord shortly after entry, so unilateral cord injury causes contralateral pain-temperature loss beginning slightly below the lesion.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use spinal-tract crossing anatomy to explain the characteristic ipsilateral motor/proprioceptive and contralateral pain-temperature deficits of Brown-Sequard syndrome.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: IgG autoantibodies target desmoglein adhesion molecules within desmosomes, disrupting keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion. The resulting acantholysis produces fragile intraepidermal blisters, mucosal erosions, and a positive Nikolsky sign.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect flaccid bullae, mucosal erosions, positive Nikolsky sign, and suprabasal acantholysis to IgG-mediated disruption of desmoglein-containing desmosomes.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: LYST regulates lysosomal and lysosome-related organelle trafficking, size, and fission. Loss of function produces enlarged fused lysosomal granules in leukocytes and other cells, impairing neutrophil antimicrobial function and cytotoxic-cell degranulation while also disrupting melanosomes and platelet dense granules.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Chediak-Higashi syndrome from recurrent pyogenic infections, partial albinism, bleeding tendency, and giant leukocyte granules and connect it to defective LYST-mediated lysosomal trafficking.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: 5-alpha-reductase type 2 converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone. DHT is particularly important for masculinization of the external genitalia during embryogenesis. Deficiency causes undervirilized external genitalia in a 46,XY individual despite preserved anti-Müllerian hormone activity; rising testosterone at puberty can produce partial virilization.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize 5-alpha-reductase deficiency and identify the impaired conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone as the biochemical defect.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC39A4 encodes the ZIP4 zinc uptake transporter in the small intestine. Autosomal-recessive loss of function impairs enteral zinc absorption, producing zinc deficiency with periorificial/acral dermatitis, alopecia, diarrhea, impaired wound healing, and immune dysfunction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize acrodermatitis enteropathica after weaning and connect the phenotype to loss of the SLC39A4-encoded intestinal ZIP4 zinc transporter.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Organophosphates phosphorylate and inhibit acetylcholinesterase, causing acetylcholine accumulation at muscarinic, nicotinic, and central synapses. With time, the phosphorylated enzyme undergoes aging, strengthening the bond so oxime reactivation is no longer effective; pralidoxime is therefore most useful before aging occurs.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain why pralidoxime must be given early in organophosphate poisoning by linking treatment efficacy to aging of phosphorylated acetylcholinesterase.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: WASp links hematopoietic-cell signaling to actin-cytoskeleton remodeling. Loss of WASp disrupts immune-cell migration, phagocytosis, and immunologic-synapse formation and is associated with characteristically small platelets and thrombocytopenia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome from eczema, recurrent infections, and small-platelet thrombocytopenia and connect the phenotype to defective WASp-mediated actin-cytoskeleton remodeling.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants in desmosomal genes such as PKP2 weaken mechanical coupling between cardiomyocytes. Recurrent mechanical stress promotes myocyte injury and progressive fibrofatty myocardial replacement, creating a substrate for ventricular arrhythmias.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and connect its fibrofatty arrhythmogenic substrate to inherited defects in cardiomyocyte desmosomes.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Catechol-O-methyltransferase methylates catecholamines to metanephrine and normetanephrine. These metabolites have longer effective persistence than episodically secreted catecholamines, making fractionated metanephrines useful biochemical markers of pheochromocytoma.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect pheochromocytoma biochemical testing to catechol-O-methyltransferase–mediated formation of metanephrine and normetanephrine.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Autoantibodies bind hemidesmosomal proteins BP180 (type XVII collagen/BPAG2) and BP230 (BPAG1) at the dermal-epidermal junction. Complement and inflammatory-cell activation damage the basement-membrane zone, producing a subepidermal blister with tense bullae.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate bullous pemphigoid from intraepidermal blistering diseases by linking tense subepidermal bullae and linear IgG/C3 to BP180/BP230 hemidesmosomal autoimmunity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Loss of NPC1 or NPC2 function disrupts intracellular trafficking of lysosomal lipid cargo, causing accumulation of unesterified cholesterol, glycosphingolipids, and gangliosides within lysosomes and progressive visceral and neurologic disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Niemann-Pick type C and connect its characteristic neurologic-visceral phenotype to NPC1/NPC2-dependent lysosomal lipid-trafficking failure.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Vitamin B12 is required for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase to convert methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA. Deficiency causes methylmalonic acid and related metabolites to accumulate and contributes to abnormal myelin lipid synthesis, producing posterior-column and corticospinal-tract dysfunction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect subacute combined degeneration and megaloblastic anemia to vitamin B12 deficiency and recognize elevated methylmalonic acid as a specific metabolic consequence.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A participant who has not experienced the event when observation ends contributes information to the risk set through the last known event-free time and is then censored. Excluding the participant entirely discards valid follow-up information, whereas counting censoring as an event falsely lowers estimated survival.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Apply right-censoring rules in Kaplan-Meier analysis by retaining observed follow-up through the censoring time without treating censoring as the outcome event.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Decision-making capacity is a clinical, decision-specific functional assessment. A capable patient can understand relevant information, appreciate how it applies personally, reason about options and consequences, and communicate a stable choice; agreement with the clinician's recommendation is not required.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish medical decision-making capacity from agreement with treatment recommendations and recognize the functional abilities required for a capable refusal.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A lysogenic bacteriophage supplies the tox gene. The diphtheria toxin A fragment transfers ADP-ribose from NAD to elongation factor 2, inactivating EF-2 and halting eukaryotic protein synthesis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify elongation factor 2 as the direct host-cell target of diphtheria toxin and distinguish this mechanism from other classic bacterial exotoxins.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants in HMBS reduce porphobilinogen deaminase activity, the third enzyme of heme synthesis. Induction of hepatic ALA synthase during attacks increases upstream neurotoxic precursors such as ALA and porphobilinogen, causing episodic neurovisceral symptoms without the photosensitive cutaneous manifestations seen in porphyrias that accumulate later porphyrins.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize acute intermittent porphyria from neurovisceral attacks without photosensitivity and identify hydroxymethylbilane synthase/porphobilinogen deaminase as the deficient enzyme.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Federal disability-rights requirements call for communication with patients with vision disabilities to be as effective as communication with others. When necessary, covered health programs should provide appropriate auxiliary aids or services such as qualified readers, Braille, large print, or accessible electronic formats, with the choice guided by effective communication and the individual's needs.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Apply disability-access principles by selecting an effective accessible format for a patient with visual impairment rather than relying on family members, inaccessible standard print, waivers, or reduced information.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Pathogenic variants in genes such as AGPAT2 or BSCL2 impair adipocyte development or function and prevent normal storage of triglyceride in adipose tissue. The resulting near-total loss of body fat causes ectopic lipid deposition, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance/diabetes, and fatty liver.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize congenital generalized lipodystrophy from near-total loss of adipose tissue with a muscular appearance, hypertriglyceridemia, insulin resistance, and hepatomegaly.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PLP1 variants disrupt proteolipid protein 1/DM20 production, folding, trafficking, or availability in oligodendrocyte membranes. Because these proteins are major components of central nervous system myelin, the result is hypomyelination and progressive neurologic dysfunction, usually in males with X-linked inheritance.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease from early nystagmus, motor delay, diffuse hypomyelination, and an X-linked family pattern.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PAX2 encodes a transcription factor required for normal embryonic development of the kidneys and eyes. Loss of functional PAX2 can disrupt formation of renal tissue and the optic nerve, producing congenital kidney abnormalities with optic nerve coloboma; inheritance is autosomal dominant when a pathogenic PAX2 variant is present.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize renal coloboma syndrome from congenital kidney disease plus optic nerve coloboma and connect the phenotype to PAX2-dependent embryonic development.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ATP2C1 encodes hSPCA1, an ATP-powered pump that transports calcium and manganese into the Golgi apparatus. Loss of functional hSPCA1 disrupts Golgi calcium storage in keratinocytes, impairing cell adhesion and making the epidermis fragile in areas exposed to heat, moisture, and friction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect Hailey-Hailey disease caused by ATP2C1 variants to defective ATP-dependent calcium transport into the Golgi apparatus.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Activating GLUD1 variants cause hyperactive glutamate dehydrogenase. Increased glutamate oxidation generates ammonia and alpha-ketoglutarate; alpha-ketoglutarate enters the citric acid cycle, increases the ATP-to-ADP ratio in pancreatic beta cells, and stimulates insulin secretion. Leucine allosterically activates glutamate dehydrogenase, explaining protein-triggered hypoglycemia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize GLUD1-related hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome from protein-sensitive hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and persistent mild hyperammonemia.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Activating germline LHCGR variants cause ligand-independent signaling through the LH/chorionic-gonadotropin receptor in Leydig cells. Autonomous receptor activity drives testosterone production despite suppressed pituitary gonadotropins, producing gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty in young boys; the phenotype is male-limited and commonly inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish familial male-limited precocious puberty from central and other peripheral causes of precocity by recognizing high testosterone with suppressed gonadotropins, negative hCG testing, and a male-limited familial pattern.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GCH1 encodes GTP cyclohydrolase 1, which catalyzes the first of three steps in tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis. Reduced GCH1 activity lowers tetrahydrobiopterin availability, impairing dopamine synthesis and producing childhood-onset dystonia with diurnal fluctuation and marked response to levodopa.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect GCH1-related dopa-responsive dystonia with impaired tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis and reduced dopamine production.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CSF2RA encodes the alpha subunit of the GM-CSF receptor. Loss of effective GM-CSF signaling impairs terminal function of alveolar macrophages, particularly surfactant catabolism and clearance, causing intra-alveolar surfactant accumulation and hypoxemic respiratory disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect CSF2RA-related hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis with impaired GM-CSF-dependent surfactant clearance by alveolar macrophages.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: KRT6A encodes keratin 6a, which pairs with keratin 16 to assemble keratin intermediate filaments. These intracellular networks provide mechanical strength and resilience to nail, palmoplantar, and oral epithelial cells; pathogenic KRT6A variants disrupt filament assembly and produce friction-induced tissue fragility and hyperkeratosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect KRT6A-related pachyonychia congenita with defective keratin intermediate-filament assembly and epithelial mechanical fragility.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The SPIKES framework structures delivery of serious news as Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Empathy, and Summary/Strategy. After establishing a private setting and assessing the patient’s perception, the clinician should obtain the patient’s invitation by determining how much information the patient wants before giving detailed knowledge.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Apply the SPIKES sequence by obtaining the patient’s invitation and information preference after assessing perception and before delivering detailed serious news.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function CASR variants make the calcium-sensing receptor abnormally sensitive to extracellular calcium. CaSR signaling is therefore activated at lower calcium concentrations, suppressing parathyroid hormone release and promoting renal calcium excretion despite systemic hypocalcemia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish activating from inactivating CaSR disorders by recognizing that gain-of-function CASR variants suppress PTH and renal calcium reabsorption at abnormally low serum calcium concentrations.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC2A1 encodes GLUT1, the facilitated glucose transporter that carries glucose across blood-brain-barrier endothelial cells. Reduced GLUT1 activity limits cerebral glucose delivery despite normal systemic glucose, producing hypoglycorrhachia and neurologic manifestations such as childhood seizures and paroxysmal exercise- or fasting-related movement abnormalities.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect SLC2A1/GLUT1 deficiency, hypoglycorrhachia with normal serum glucose, and neurologic symptoms to impaired facilitated glucose transport across the blood-brain barrier.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: BSND encodes barttin, an essential beta subunit required for trafficking and function of ClC-Ka and ClC-Kb chloride channels. In the thick ascending limb, loss of barttin impairs basolateral chloride exit and salt reabsorption, producing renal salt wasting, secondary hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and low-to-normal blood pressure. The same ClC-K channel complex in the inner ear explains congenital sensorineural hearing loss.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link BSND/barttin dysfunction to impaired ClC-Ka/ClC-Kb channel function and recognize Bartter type IV from antenatal salt wasting plus sensorineural hearing loss.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ALPL encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNSALP). Reduced TNSALP activity causes persistently low serum alkaline-phosphatase activity and accumulation of inorganic pyrophosphate, an inhibitor of hydroxyapatite mineralization, resulting in defective skeletal and dental mineralization.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize hypophosphatasia from persistently low alkaline phosphatase, defective bone mineralization and premature root-intact tooth loss, and relate it to ALPL/TNSALP deficiency and pyrophosphate accumulation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: The NURSE framework structures empathic responses to emotion as Name, Understand, Respect, Support, and Explore. When a patient directly expresses fear, naming the emotion explicitly before redirecting to biomedical information validates the emotional cue and facilitates subsequent communication.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Respond to a patient's strong emotional cue with explicit empathic acknowledgment using the NURSE framework rather than reassurance, confrontation, or immediate information dumping.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic loss-of-function MC2R variants impair the adrenal ACTH receptor. The adrenal cortex therefore cannot respond normally to ACTH to generate glucocorticoids, causing very low cortisol with markedly elevated ACTH and hyperpigmentation. Mineralocorticoid secretion is classically preserved, distinguishing isolated ACTH resistance from global primary adrenal destruction or many steroidogenic defects.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize familial glucocorticoid deficiency from childhood hypoglycemia, hyperpigmentation, low cortisol, very high ACTH, and preserved mineralocorticoid function and connect it to MC2R-mediated ACTH resistance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Alexander disease is an astrocytopathy caused by heterozygous gain-of-function GFAP variants. Mutant glial fibrillary acidic protein, an astrocytic intermediate filament, aggregates and contributes to formation of Rosenthal fibers, with associated white-matter dysfunction, especially in early-onset cerebral disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect infantile Alexander disease and Rosenthal fibers with gain-of-function GFAP dysfunction in astrocytic intermediate filaments.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Claudin-16 is a tight-junction protein in the thick ascending limb that contributes to paracellular reabsorption of divalent cations. CLDN16 dysfunction reduces paracellular magnesium and calcium reabsorption, causing renal magnesium wasting, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis/nephrolithiasis and progressive kidney dysfunction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize CLDN16-related familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis and localize the defect to paracellular divalent-cation reabsorption in the thick ascending limb.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Phosphaturic mesenchymal tumors can secrete excess FGF23. FGF23 decreases proximal tubular sodium-phosphate cotransporter expression and suppresses renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity, producing renal phosphate wasting, hypophosphatemia, low or inappropriately normal calcitriol, and defective bone mineralization.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize tumor-induced osteomalacia as an FGF23-mediated renal phosphate-wasting disorder with inappropriately low calcitriol and defective bone mineralization.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Chunk-and-check reduces cognitive load by presenting a small amount of information at a time and confirming comprehension before moving to the next segment. It differs from a single end-of-visit yes/no check because misunderstanding is identified and corrected iteratively.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use chunk-and-check to teach a complex care plan by delivering information in small segments and verifying comprehension after each segment.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: A warm handoff transfers care face to face between health professionals in front of the patient, treating the patient as a team member who can hear, clarify, correct, and ask questions. This provides a safety check against omissions or distortions during transitions.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use a patient-engaged warm handoff for an in-practice transition of care when both clinicians are available.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: An active-listening summary condenses the patient's story and explicitly checks accuracy. It demonstrates attention, exposes misunderstanding, and lets the patient correct the clinician before diagnostic or counseling decisions are made.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use a concise summary followed by an accuracy check to demonstrate active listening and verify the patient's narrative.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Eliciting the patient's explanatory model identifies beliefs about cause, course, consequences, and preferred treatment. This reveals potential discordance between the medical plan and the patient's beliefs and allows counseling to be tailored rather than assuming nonadherence or dismissing beliefs.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Elicit a patient's explanatory model before attempting to reconcile health beliefs with an evidence-based treatment plan.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Family involvement should be guided by the patient's preferences when the patient has capacity. The clinician should preserve patient participation and privacy while allowing supportive family involvement to the extent the patient desires.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Preserve patient autonomy by asking a capable patient how they want a family companion involved before assigning the companion a role in communication or decisions.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GCM2 is a transcription factor and master regulator of parathyroid development. Loss-of-function variants can impair parathyroid development or function, producing inappropriately low PTH, hypocalcemia, and hyperphosphatemia without the broader phenotype of syndromic hypoparathyroidism.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect GCM2 loss of function with defective parathyroid development and familial isolated hypoparathyroidism.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Germline gain-of-function variants in TSHR can constitutively activate TSH-receptor signaling in thyroid follicular cells, increasing thyroid hormone synthesis and growth despite suppressed pituitary TSH and absent stimulating autoantibodies.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize constitutive TSH-receptor activation as the mechanism of autosomal-dominant antibody-negative familial hyperthyroidism.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function KCNJ5 variants reduce potassium-channel selectivity so sodium enters zona glomerulosa cells. Membrane depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels; increased intracellular calcium activates signaling that increases aldosterone synthesis and can promote adrenal hyperplasia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Trace the ion-channel mechanism linking KCNJ5 loss of potassium selectivity to calcium-dependent aldosterone excess.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CYP11B2, expressed in the zona glomerulosa, catalyzes the terminal mitochondrial reactions converting deoxycorticosterone derivatives to aldosterone. Inactivating variants cause isolated hypoaldosteronism with salt wasting and high renin while cortisol and sex-steroid synthesis remain intact.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate isolated CYP11B2 aldosterone synthase deficiency from other steroidogenic enzyme defects using renin, aldosterone, cortisol, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and blood-pressure patterns.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: STAR normally mediates the rate-limiting transfer of cholesterol into mitochondria for steroidogenesis. Severe STAR deficiency causes profound reduction of adrenal and gonadal steroids; compensatory trophic stimulation drives cholesterol accumulation and progressive steroidogenic-cell injury.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize STAR-related lipoid congenital adrenal hyperplasia from global steroid deficiency, salt wasting, 46,XY undervirilization, and lipid-laden enlarged adrenals.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CACNA1A encodes the alpha-1A subunit of the presynaptic CaV2.1 P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channel. EA2 commonly results from loss-of-function variants that disturb cerebellar neurotransmission, causing hours-long attacks of ataxia/vertigo with interictal nystagmus and often response to acetazolamide.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Associate hours-long episodic ataxia with interictal nystagmus and acetazolamide response with CACNA1A/P/Q-type calcium-channel dysfunction.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GLRA1 encodes the alpha-1 subunit of the inhibitory glycine receptor, a ligand-gated chloride channel concentrated in brainstem and spinal-cord circuits. Impaired glycinergic inhibition produces neonatal hypertonia and an exaggerated generalized startle response to unexpected stimuli.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize hereditary hyperekplexia from neonatal hypertonia, preserved consciousness, stimulus-triggered nonhabituating startle, and normal EEG during events.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Heterozygous PRRT2 variants disturb presynaptic neurotransmitter release and cause brief paroxysmal dyskinesias triggered by sudden voluntary movement. Attacks usually last seconds to under a minute, consciousness is preserved, examination is normal between attacks, and carbamazepine often suppresses events.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect classic paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia with PRRT2-dependent presynaptic neurotransmission.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ATP1A3 encodes a neuronal Na+/K+-ATPase alpha subunit. Pathogenic variants can produce alternating hemiplegia of childhood, with onset before 18 months, recurrent hemiplegic or quadriplegic episodes, dystonia/abnormal eye movements, developmental abnormalities, and a characteristic improvement or remission of attacks during sleep.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize ATP1A3-related alternating hemiplegia of childhood from early onset, alternating hemiplegia, developmental abnormalities, and sleep-dependent spell remission.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: FOLR1 encodes folate receptor alpha at the choroid plexus. Loss of function impairs folate transport across the blood-choroid-plexus-CSF barrier, producing very low CSF folate despite normal systemic folate and later-onset developmental regression, seizures, movement abnormalities, and hypomyelination.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish FOLR1 cerebral folate transport deficiency from systemic folate deficiency by recognizing very low CSF folate with normal serum folate and blood counts.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC34A3 encodes the proximal-tubule sodium-phosphate cotransporter NaPi-IIc. Loss of function causes renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia. The low phosphate appropriately stimulates 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, increasing intestinal calcium absorption and producing hypercalciuria—a key discriminator from FGF23-mediated hypophosphatemic disorders.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize SLC34A3/NaPi-IIc loss as the cause of hypophosphatemic rickets with elevated calcitriol and hypercalciuria.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GRHPR deficiency impairs glyoxylate reduction and hydroxypyruvate metabolism, increasing endogenous oxalate production. PH2 causes recurrent calcium-oxalate stones/nephrocalcinosis and characteristically increased urinary L-glycerate; biallelic GRHPR variants establish the diagnosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Use elevated urinary L-glycerate to identify GRHPR-related primary hyperoxaluria type 2 among inherited hyperoxalurias.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Xanthine dehydrogenase catalyzes the final two steps of purine degradation: hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. XDH loss therefore causes profound hypouricemia/hypouricosuria with xanthine accumulation and xanthine nephrolithiasis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect XDH deficiency with failure of terminal purine oxidation, profound hypouricemia, and xanthine nephrolithiasis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function AVPR2 variants constitutively activate the renal vasopressin V2 receptor in collecting-duct principal cells even without AVP. Persistent cAMP-dependent aquaporin-2 trafficking increases free-water reabsorption, causing hypotonic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine and suppressed endogenous vasopressin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish activating AVPR2-associated NSIAD from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and SIADH by using hormone level, serum tonicity, and urine concentration.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: TRPM6 channels mediate magnesium absorption in intestine and magnesium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule. Loss of function causes profound hypomagnesemia; severe magnesium deficiency suppresses PTH secretion and impairs PTH action, producing secondary hypocalcemia and neuromuscular irritability.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize TRPM6 deficiency as a combined intestinal and renal magnesium-transport defect that causes secondary hypocalcemia through severe magnesium depletion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ATP2A2 encodes SERCA2, an endoplasmic-reticulum Ca2+-ATPase that pumps cytosolic calcium into the ER. Reduced SERCA2 function disrupts intracellular calcium homeostasis and calcium-dependent keratinocyte adhesion/differentiation, causing acantholytic dyskeratosis and greasy hyperkeratotic papules.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect ATP2A2/SERCA2 dysfunction in Darier disease with impaired endoplasmic-reticulum calcium sequestration and keratinocyte adhesion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: FERMT1 encodes kindlin-1, a focal-adhesion adaptor involved in integrin-associated signaling and linkage of actin to membrane adhesion complexes. Loss causes mixed-level skin fragility with acral blistering early in life, childhood photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma and skin atrophy, plus mucosal disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize Kindler epidermolysis bullosa from the combination of early trauma-induced blistering, photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma/atrophy, mucosal disease, and FERMT1 variants.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ENPP1 converts extracellular ATP to AMP and inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi). PPi is a potent inhibitor of hydroxyapatite deposition. ENPP1 deficiency lowers extracellular PPi, permitting pathologic mineral deposition in arterial walls and causing infantile arterial calcification and stenosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link ENPP1 deficiency in generalized arterial calcification of infancy to reduced extracellular pyrophosphate and loss of hydroxyapatite inhibition.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic HPGD or SLCO2A1 variants can cause primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. HPGD loss reduces enzymatic PGE2 degradation, while SLCO2A1 loss impairs cellular prostaglandin uptake needed for clearance. Both mechanisms increase PGE2 exposure and produce digital clubbing, periostosis, arthropathy, and pachydermia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect hereditary pachydermoperiostosis with impaired HPGD/SLCO2A1-dependent prostaglandin E2 clearance rather than secondary cardiopulmonary clubbing.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SPINK5 encodes LEKT1, a serine-protease inhibitor in the epidermis. Loss of LEKT1 permits excessive epidermal protease activity, disrupting stratum-corneum barrier proteins and producing ichthyosis, hair-shaft defects such as trichorrhexis invaginata, and marked atopy.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link SPINK5/LEKT1 deficiency in Netherton syndrome to excessive epidermal serine-protease activity and impaired skin-barrier integrity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: COQ8A-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency impairs mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect biallelic COQ8A loss with primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency and impaired mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CSF1R signaling regulates microglial survival, proliferation, differentiation, and function
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize CSF1R as a receptor tyrosine kinase critical for microglial survival and function in CSF1R-related leukoencephalopathy.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SMN2 copy number as a severity modifier in spinal muscular atrophy
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize SMN2 copy number as an important modifier of spinal muscular atrophy severity because additional copies generate more functional SMN protein.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GJB1/connexin-32 gap-junction function in Schwann cells in CMT1X
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect GJB1 loss in CMT1X with impaired connexin-32 gap-junction communication in Schwann cells.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC9A6 encodes endosomal NHE6, a Na+/H+ exchanger that regulates intra-endosomal pH
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize SLC9A6/NHE6 as an endosomal sodium-hydrogen exchanger required for normal endosomal pH regulation in Christianson syndrome.
construct_inventory.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CDC73 encodes nuclear parafibromin, a tumor suppressor involved in transcriptional regulation and control of proliferation
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect CDC73 loss to deficient nuclear parafibromin tumor-suppressor activity in hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: KATP-channel mechanism of congenital hyperinsulinism
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Trace congenital hyperinsulinism from loss of beta-cell KATP-channel activity to depolarization, calcium influx, and inappropriate insulin secretion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Glucokinase as beta-cell glucose sensor in GCK-MODY
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize glucokinase as a beta-cell glucose sensor and GCK-MODY as an upward shift in the glucose threshold for insulin secretion.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NR0B1/DAX1 regulates development and function of adrenal and reproductive endocrine tissues
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize NR0B1/DAX1 as a developmental regulator of adrenal and hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal tissues in X-linked adrenal hypoplasia congenita.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CYP24A1 encodes vitamin D 24-hydroxylase that inactivates calcitriol and 25-hydroxyvitamin D
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize CYP24A1 loss as impaired vitamin-D 24-hydroxylation and catabolism, causing infantile hypercalcemia and nephrocalcinosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: AIRE-dependent tissue-restricted self-antigen expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells enables central negative selection
construct_inventory.educational_objective: AIRE promotes tissue-restricted self-antigen expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells, enabling central negative selection; loss permits autoreactive T cells to escape and causes APECED.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: TAP1/TAP2 transport cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading
construct_inventory.educational_objective: TAP1/TAP2 use ATP to transport cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading; TAP deficiency lowers surface MHC I and can produce selective CD8+ T-cell lymphopenia.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Complete IL2RG loss causes T-B+NK- X-SCID through loss of common-gamma-chain signaling, particularly IL-7 for T-cell and IL-15 for NK-cell development
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Complete IL2RG loss causes T-B+NK- X-linked SCID because common-gamma-chain cytokine signaling is disrupted; loss of IL-7 signaling arrests T-cell development and loss of IL-15 signaling arrests NK-cell development.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ZAP70 transduces signals downstream of activated TCR/CD3 complexes; loss causes impaired TCR-mediated activation with preserved response to downstream pharmacologic bypass
construct_inventory.educational_objective: ZAP70 deficiency impairs signaling downstream of the TCR/CD3 complex, producing severely reduced CD8+ T cells and dysfunctional CD4+ T cells; preserved response to PMA/ionomycin localizes the defect proximal to those downstream second messengers.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: MYD88 is a shared intracellular adaptor for most Toll-like receptors and most IL-1 receptor family members; loss predisposes to invasive pyogenic bacterial infection
construct_inventory.educational_objective: MYD88 is the shared adaptor for most Toll-like receptor and most IL-1 receptor family signaling; loss impairs early innate inflammatory responses and predisposes to recurrent invasive pyogenic bacterial infection.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Recognition of LMNA-related dilated cardiomyopathy from autosomal-dominant conduction disease preceding ventricular dysfunction
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize LMNA-related dilated cardiomyopathy when progressive conduction-system disease precedes nonischemic ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction in an autosomal-dominant family.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: BAG3-related dilated cardiomyopathy due to impaired chaperone-assisted selective autophagy and cardiomyocyte proteostasis
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link BAG3-related cardiomyopathy to defective chaperone-dependent protein quality control and selective autophagy in cardiomyocytes.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Recognition of HCN4-related familial sinus bradycardia associated with left ventricular noncompaction
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize HCN4-related disease when autosomal-dominant sinus bradycardia co-segregates with left ventricular noncompaction.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NKX2-5 as a cardiac homeobox transcription factor causing atrial septal defect with progressive atrioventricular conduction disease
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Associate familial atrial septal defects plus progressive AV conduction disease with NKX2-5, a homeobox transcription factor involved in cardiac development.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Junctophilin-2 maintains cardiac plasma-membrane/T-tubule to sarcoplasmic-reticulum junctions required for excitation-contraction coupling
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Understand that junctophilin-2 organizes cardiac dyads, bringing T-tubular calcium-entry channels into close proximity with SR calcium-release channels for excitation-contraction coupling.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Recognition of ATP8B1 deficiency/PFIC1 from low-GGT cholestasis plus extrahepatic diarrhea and hearing involvement
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate ATP8B1/PFIC1 from other inherited cholestatic disorders by recognizing low/normal GGT cholestasis accompanied by extrahepatic manifestations such as diarrhea and hearing loss.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Recognition of NEUROG3-related enteric anendocrinosis from congenital malabsorptive diarrhea with selective absence of intestinal enteroendocrine cells and emerging diabetes
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize NEUROG3-related enteric anendocrinosis when congenital malabsorptive diarrhea occurs with preserved major epithelial lineages but marked absence of enteroendocrine cells, particularly when diabetes emerges.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Recognition of VPS33B-related arthrogryposis-renal dysfunction-cholestasis syndrome
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize VPS33B-related ARC syndrome from the triad of arthrogryposis, renal tubular dysfunction, and low-GGT neonatal cholestasis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC51B/OST-beta deficiency impairs basolateral export of bile acids from ileal enterocytes into portal circulation
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Map SLC51B/OST-beta to basolateral ileal bile-acid export in the enterohepatic circulation, distinguishing it from ASBT, BSEP, NTCP, and NPC1L1.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Recognition of HSD3B7 deficiency from low-GGT neonatal cholestasis with low primary bile acids and diagnostic 3beta-hydroxy-delta5 intermediates
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish HSD3B7 bile-acid synthesis deficiency from low-GGT bile-transport disorders by recognizing low primary bile acids plus characteristic atypical 3beta-hydroxy-delta5 intermediates.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: WHIM syndrome results from gain-of-function CXCR4 signaling with impaired receptor downregulation, causing CXCL12-mediated marrow retention (myelokathexis) and peripheral neutropenia.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize that WHIM syndrome is a leukocyte-trafficking disorder in which gain-of-function CXCR4 signaling causes CXCL12-mediated marrow retention of mature leukocytes and peripheral neutropenia.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GATA2 deficiency (MonoMAC/DCML spectrum) is recognized by invasive nontuberculous mycobacterial disease, HPV susceptibility, monocytopenia with B/NK-cell deficiency, and myelodysplasia/myeloid-malignancy predisposition.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize GATA2 deficiency when invasive nontuberculous mycobacterial or HPV disease occurs with monocytopenia, B/NK-cell deficiency, and myelodysplastic or AML predisposition.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: DADA2 should be recognized in a child with livedo racemosa, systemic vasculitis/vasculopathy, hypertension, early lacunar strokes, hematologic abnormalities, and recessive familial clustering.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish DADA2 from sporadic polyarteritis nodosa and other inflammatory disorders when childhood livedoid vasculopathy, hypertension, strokes, hematologic abnormalities, and recessive familial clustering occur together.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PIK3CD gain-of-function in APDS1 causes hyperactivation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, disrupting normal B- and T-cell maturation and function.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connect PIK3CD gain-of-function mutations in activated PI3K-delta syndrome to PI3K-AKT-mTOR hyperactivation and abnormal lymphocyte maturation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Inherited C1q deficiency strongly predisposes to early SLE in part because impaired recognition/opsonization and clearance of apoptotic material increases exposure to self-antigens and loss of tolerance.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain the paradox that deficiency of an early classical complement component can cause autoimmunity: failure to clear apoptotic material increases persistent self-antigen exposure and promotes loss of tolerance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PNPLA1 is a keratinocyte transacylase required for omega-O-acylceramide synthesis; loss impairs the stratum-corneum lipid barrier and causes autosomal-recessive congenital ichthyosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link PNPLA1-associated congenital ichthyosis to failure of omega-O-acylceramide synthesis, specifically transfer of linoleate to omega-hydroxyceramide in differentiated keratinocytes.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: KLHL24 start-codon variants stabilize a gain-of-function ubiquitin-ligase substrate adaptor, causing excessive ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of keratin 14 and an EBS phenotype that can include cardiomyopathy.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize a nonstructural cause of epidermolysis bullosa: KLHL24 gain of function increases ubiquitin-proteasome degradation of keratin 14 rather than directly mutating the keratin filament.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic PKP1 loss causes ectodermal dysplasia-skin fragility syndrome, characterized by trauma-induced erosions, hair/nail/sweat abnormalities, palmoplantar keratoderma, and poorly formed desmosomes with weak keratin attachment.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize plakophilin 1 deficiency from trauma-induced skin fragility, ectodermal abnormalities, palmoplantar keratoderma, and malformed desmosomes with poor keratin-filament attachment.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Autosomal-recessive CDSN loss causes generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome with superficial peeling, pruritus, atopy, and epidermal-barrier failure; normal LEKT1 and hair findings help exclude Netherton syndrome.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate CDSN-related generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome from Netherton and other peeling/ichthyotic disorders by lifelong generalized superficial peeling, severe atopy, normal LEKT1, and normal hair microscopy.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic PLEC variants cause epidermolysis bullosa simplex with muscular dystrophy because plectin mechanically couples intermediate-filament networks in basal keratinocytes and muscle.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize PLEC-associated EBS with muscular dystrophy when lifelong basal-keratinocyte skin fragility is followed by progressive myopathy, reflecting plectin's role as an intermediate-filament cytoskeletal linker in both tissues.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: HNF1B haploinsufficiency causes a multisystem developmental disorder in which renal cystic/structural disease commonly coexists with renal magnesium wasting, pancreatic abnormalities, early-onset nonautoimmune diabetes, and genital-tract malformations.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize HNF1B-related disease from the syndromic combination of renal structural disease, hypomagnesemia, pancreatic abnormalities, nonautoimmune diabetes, and genital-tract malformations.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: EYA1 variants are a major cause of autosomal-dominant branchio-oto-renal syndrome, characterized by branchial arch anomalies, preauricular/ear malformations, hearing loss, and renal abnormalities.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize EYA1-related branchio-oto-renal syndrome from the combination of branchial anomalies, preauricular pits, hearing loss, renal abnormalities, and autosomal-dominant inheritance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ADTKD-MUC1 is caused by MUC1 VNTR frameshift mutations that generate a toxic frameshifted MUC1 protein (MUC1fs), producing progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Understand that MUC1 VNTR frameshift mutations cause ADTKD by producing a toxic frameshifted MUC1 protein in tubular epithelial cells.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC34A2 encodes the type IIb sodium-phosphate cotransporter; loss of function causes pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis with accumulation of calcium-phosphate microliths in alveoli.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Understand that SLC34A2 loss impairs epithelial phosphate transport in the lung and causes calcium-phosphate microlith accumulation in pulmonary alveoli.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: ABCA3 is a phospholipid transporter in type II pneumocytes required for transport and organization of surfactant lipids within lamellar bodies; loss of function causes severe neonatal surfactant dysfunction or later interstitial lung disease.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Know that ABCA3 transports surfactant phospholipids into lamellar bodies of type II pneumocytes and that loss of function causes inherited surfactant dysfunction.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: PROP1 loss is a major genetic cause of combined pituitary hormone deficiency, typically affecting GH and TSH and later gonadotropins; ACTH deficiency can emerge over time.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize PROP1-related combined pituitary hormone deficiency as a progressive, multi-lineage anterior pituitary disorder that can evolve from GH/TSH deficiency to gonadotropin and sometimes ACTH deficiency.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Inactivating FSHR variants cause gonadotropin resistance with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism/ovarian failure and impaired follicular maturation in 46,XX individuals.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize FSH-receptor resistance as a rare cause of hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, primary amenorrhea, and arrested follicular maturation in 46,XX patients.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: IGF1R loss causes target-tissue resistance to IGF-1, often with prenatal and postnatal growth failure and elevated IGF-1; receptor autophosphorylation and downstream signaling are impaired.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Differentiate IGF-1 resistance from GH resistance: IGF1R defects cause prenatal/postnatal growth failure with normal or elevated IGF-1 and impaired receptor signaling.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: MRAP is an accessory protein required for normal trafficking and function of the ACTH receptor MC2R; loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 2 with ACTH resistance and usually preserved mineralocorticoids.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Know that MRAP is required for MC2R trafficking/function and that MRAP loss causes familial glucocorticoid deficiency with isolated ACTH resistance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Triple-A (Allgrove) syndrome is an autosomal-recessive AAAS disorder characterized by alacrima, achalasia, ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, and often progressive neurologic dysfunction.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize triple-A syndrome from alacrima, achalasia, adrenal insufficiency, and neurologic dysfunction, and associate it with pathogenic AAAS variants affecting ALADIN.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NR1H4/FXR-related PFIC recognition
construct_inventory.educational_objective: FXR deficiency from NR1H4 loss can present as severe neonatal low-GGT cholestasis with high alpha-fetoprotein and reduced BSEP expression despite no ABCB11 mutation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Activating GUCY2C mutation causing cGMP-mediated CFTR chloride secretion
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Activating intestinal guanylate cyclase C causes a cGMP-driven secretory diarrhea through increased epithelial chloride and water secretion, including CFTR activation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CTRC loss reduces protective trypsinogen degradation
construct_inventory.educational_objective: CTRC protects the pancreas by degrading trypsinogen; loss of CTRC function permits excessive intrapancreatic trypsin activity and increases chronic pancreatitis risk.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC10A1/NTCP deficiency causing isolated hypercholanemia
construct_inventory.educational_objective: NTCP deficiency should be recognized when very high circulating bile acids occur with relatively preserved liver function; SLC10A1 encodes the major hepatocyte uptake transporter for conjugated bile salts.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Johanson-Blizzard syndrome from UBR1 deficiency
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Associate congenital exocrine pancreatic insufficiency and hypoplastic nasal alae with UBR1-related Johanson-Blizzard syndrome.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: FLNC truncating-variant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibrosis and cell-cell adhesion disruption
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Truncating FLNC variants can cause cardiac-restricted arrhythmogenic dilated cardiomyopathy characterized by myocardial fibrosis and disruption of cytoskeletal/intercalated-disc integrity, creating a substrate for ventricular arrhythmias.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: TRDN-related recessive catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize TRDN as a cause of autosomal-recessive CPVT when stress-induced polymorphic/bidirectional ventricular tachycardia occurs despite a normal resting ECG and negative RYR2/CASQ2 testing.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: CALM2 long-QT mechanism through impaired calcium-dependent inactivation of L-type calcium current
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Calmodulin-associated long-QT syndrome can result from impaired calcium-dependent inactivation of L-type calcium current, producing persistent inward current and delayed repolarization.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: GJA5/connexin40 gap-junction dysfunction predisposing to atrial fibrillation
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Connexin40 forms atrial gap junctions that provide low-resistance electrical coupling; GJA5 dysfunction can impair atrial conduction and predispose to atrial fibrillation.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: NOTCH1-associated bicuspid aortic valve with premature calcific aortic valve disease
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Familial bicuspid aortic valve with premature calcification can result from pathogenic NOTCH1 variants; NOTCH signaling contributes to embryonic valve development and adult valve homeostasis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: KCNQ2 loss reduces the Kv7.2-containing neuronal M-current, a low-threshold slowly activating potassium current that normally restrains repetitive firing.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Relate loss-of-function KCNQ2 variants to reduced Kv7.2/Kv7.3 M-current and neuronal hyperexcitability.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SLC12A5 encodes neuronal KCC2; impaired KCC2 chloride extrusion raises intracellular chloride and makes GABA-A responses less hyperpolarizing.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Explain how impaired SLC12A5/KCC2-mediated chloride extrusion weakens mature neuronal GABAergic inhibition.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: DNM1 encodes dynamin-1, a neuronal mechanochemical GTPase required for membrane scission during synaptic vesicle endocytosis and recycling.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify dynamin-1 as the GTPase that mediates membrane scission during neuronal synaptic vesicle endocytosis.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: TUBB4A-associated H-ABC is identified by hypomyelination together with progressive basal-ganglia, especially putaminal, and cerebellar atrophy plus extrapyramidal and pyramidal findings.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize the MRI and movement-disorder phenotype of TUBB4A-associated H-ABC.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Autosomal dominant sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy is a focal epilepsy with brief stereotyped hypermotor or dystonic seizures arising predominantly from sleep and can be caused by CHRNA4 variants.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Distinguish autosomal dominant sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy from parasomnias using stereotypy, brief duration, clustering, and familial inheritance.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: LAD-III results from FERMT3/kindlin-3 deficiency, which prevents inside-out conformational activation of hematopoietic integrins despite preserved surface expression, causing leukocyte dysfunction and a platelet bleeding defect.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize LAD-III when leukocyte and platelet integrins are present but fail activation, producing both infections and bleeding.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: LRBA protects intracellular CTLA-4 from degradation and supports its endosomal recycling; LRBA deficiency reduces CTLA-4 availability and causes immune dysregulation.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link LRBA deficiency to defective CTLA-4 recycling, increased degradation, and combined autoimmunity/immunodeficiency.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: UNC13D encodes Munc13-4, which is essential for priming docked cytolytic granules before membrane fusion; deficiency causes familial HLH type 3 with impaired degranulation despite normal perforin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Identify Munc13-4 as the cytolytic-granule priming factor defective in familial HLH type 3.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: AP3B1 deficiency causes Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 2, characterized by oculocutaneous albinism, platelet dense-granule dysfunction/bleeding, neutropenia, and recurrent infections.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize AP3B1-associated HPS2 from the combination of albinism, platelet dense-granule deficiency, neutropenia, and recurrent infection.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Gain-of-function KCNN4 variants increase activity or calcium sensitivity of the erythrocyte Gardos potassium channel, promoting potassium loss, cell dehydration, and autosomal-dominant hereditary xerocytosis.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize KCNN4-associated hereditary xerocytosis as a dehydrating red-cell channelopathy caused by excessive Gardos-channel potassium efflux.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic PCSK1 loss causes prohormone convertase 1/3 deficiency, with severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea early in life followed by hyperphagia, obesity, and multiple endocrine processing abnormalities including elevated proinsulin.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Recognize PCSK1 deficiency from congenital malabsorptive diarrhea that evolves toward hyperphagia/obesity with biochemical evidence of defective prohormone processing.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: SECISBP2 encodes SBP2, which is required for selenocysteine incorporation during selenoprotein synthesis; partial deficiency impairs selenoproteins such as deiodinases and disrupts peripheral thyroid hormone metabolism.
construct_inventory.educational_objective: Link SECISBP2 deficiency to defective selenoprotein synthesis and reduced thyroid-hormone deiodinase activity.

construct_inventory.tested_construct: Biallelic inactivating GNRHR variants cause normosmic isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism through pituitary gonadotroph resistance to GnRH rather than impaired GnRH-neuron migration.
